goal: My wifi shows connected but there is no internet
plan: Confirm whether the machine can reach the internet at all
Flush the DNS resolver cache
Reset the wireless adapter and renew the IP lease

steps.stdout:
Windows IP Configuration

Wireless LAN adapter Wi-Fi:
   IPv4 Address. . . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.1.42
   Default Gateway . . . . . . . . . : 192.168.1.1

summary: The adapter had no DNS server assigned and a stale DHCP lease. Flushing the DNS cache, restarting the Wi-Fi adapter, and renewing the IP lease restored connectivity (ping to 8.8.8.8 now succeeds).
recommendation: If this recurs after sleep, update the Wi-Fi driver from the vendor site.

feedback.note: back online instantly

goal: Websites won't load but ping to IP addresses works - looks like DNS is broken
plan: Verify name resolution is failing while raw IP connectivity works
Set a reliable public DNS server
Flush the resolver cache and re-test

steps.stderr: Resolve-DnsName : microsoft.com : DNS name does not exist

summary: Name resolution was failing because the configured DNS server was unreachable. Setting Cloudflare/Google DNS (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) and flushing the cache restored domain resolution.
recommendation: Keep DNS set to automatic unless your network requires a specific resolver.

goal: My bluetooth headphones will not pair with the laptop
plan: Check that the Bluetooth support service is running
Confirm the Bluetooth radio is present and enabled
Restart the service so the stack re-scans for devices

steps.command: Get-Service bthserv | Select-Object Name, Status, StartType
steps.stdout:
Name    Status  StartType
----    ------  ---------
bthserv Stopped   Manual

Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     Intel(R) Wireless Bluetooth(R)

summary: The Bluetooth Support Service (bthserv) was stopped, so the pairing UI could not discover devices. Setting it to Automatic and starting it brought the stack online and the headphones paired.
recommendation: Put the headphones in pairing mode (hold the power button until the LED blinks) before adding them in Settings.

feedback.note: paired on first try after fix

goal: The bluetooth toggle disappeared from Windows settings completely
plan: Check whether the Bluetooth radio device is disabled
Re-enable the device and its service
summary: The Bluetooth radio device was in an Error/Disabled state, which removes the toggle from Settings. Re-enabling the PnP device restored the radio and the toggle reappeared.
recommendation: If the toggle vanishes again after updates, reinstall the Bluetooth driver.

goal: My PC is very slow and something is eating all the memory
plan: Identify the top memory-consuming processes
Check overall memory pressure
Advise on the offending app

steps.stdout:
Name          MB
----          --
chrome      2810
Teams       1240
explorer     540
Discord      430
SearchHost   210

summary: Chrome was holding ~2.8 GB across many tabs on an 8 GB machine with only 0.6 GB free, causing heavy paging and slowness. The system itself is healthy; the load is application-driven.
recommendation: Close unused Chrome tabs or install a tab-suspender, and consider upgrading to 16 GB RAM for comfortable multitasking.

feedback.note: much smoother after closing tabs

goal: Microphone is connected but no apps can hear my voice
plan: Check microphone privacy settings
Enable app access to microphone
summary: Microphone privacy setting was set to Deny, blocking all desktop apps from accessing the audio input. Changing the registry capability key to Allow restored microphone input.
recommendation: Check Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone if specific apps still fail.

feedback.note: mic working now

Assign a drive letter to the unassigned volume

goal: High latency and high ping spikes in online games over Wi-Fi
plan: Check background WLAN autoconfig scanning interval
Disable background Wi-Fi scanning during gameplay

steps.stdout: Auto configuration logic has been disabled on interface 'Wi-Fi'.

summary: Periodic background Wi-Fi network scanning by WLAN AutoConfig caused ping spikes. Temporarily disabling autoconfig stopped background scans during active connections.
recommendation: Remember to re-enable autoconfig when switching Wi-Fi networks.

feedback.note: lag spikes fixed

goal: Task Scheduler error prevents automated backup task from running
plan: Query task status
Start the Task Scheduler service if stopped

recommendation: Ensure Task Scheduler startup type remains on Automatic.

feedback.note: backups running now

goal: Cannot connect to local development server on port 8080
plan: Check local listening ports
Open port 8080 in Windows Firewall
summary: The local application was bound and listening on port 8080, but incoming local network traffic was blocked by Windows Firewall. Created an inbound firewall rule for TCP port 8080.

summary: TiWorker.exe (Windows Modules Installer Worker) was actively processing a pending update payload in the background, which is CPU-intensive but expected -- it is not malware.
recommendation: Let it finish (usually 20-60 minutes); if it never completes, run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' to repair the underlying update components.

goal: PC slows down noticeably after 10-15 minutes of heavy use, like it's throttling
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object Name, CurrentClockSpeed, MaxClockSpeed

summary: The processor's current clock speed had dropped well below its rated maximum during sustained load, consistent with thermal throttling protecting the chip rather than a software fault.
recommendation: Clean dust from the heatsink/fans and reapply thermal paste if the laptop/PC is a few years old; check Task Manager's Performance tab for temperature if your model exposes it.

goal: Task Manager only shows 2 cores active even though the CPU has 8
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Windows itself only sees 2 physical cores, which points to cores being disabled at the firmware level (BIOS/UEFI core count limit) rather than anything Windows can toggle.
recommendation: Enter BIOS/UEFI setup and check for a 'core limit' or 'active cores' setting under CPU configuration; reset it to 'all cores' or 'auto'.

goal: The CPU fan runs at full speed constantly, even when idle
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: CPU load itself is essentially idle, so the constant full-speed fan isn't a software load issue -- it points to a fan-curve setting stuck at 100%, often after a BIOS update or manual utility change.
recommendation: Check the fan curve in BIOS/UEFI or the vendor's fan-control utility and reset it to the default/auto profile.

goal: SysMain process uses a lot of CPU right after every boot
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: SysMain (Superfetch) was pre-loading frequently used apps into RAM right after boot, causing a short CPU/disk burst that tapers off within a couple minutes -- expected behavior, not a fault.
recommendation: If the burst is unacceptably long, disable SysMain, though on most modern SSDs it's safe to leave enabled.

goal: A generic svchost.exe process is using 40% CPU nonstop
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where-Object ProcessId -eq 4820 | Select-Object Name, DisplayName
steps.stdout:
Name   DisplayName
----   -----------
UsoSvc Update Orchestrator Service

summary: The svchost.exe instance hosting the Update Orchestrator Service (UsoSvc) was scanning/staging Windows updates in the background, accounting for the sustained CPU use.
recommendation: This normally finishes on its own; if it runs for many hours, restart the UsoSvc service or run the Windows Update troubleshooter.

goal: CPU never boosts to its rated speed, everything feels sluggish
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The system was running on the Power Saver plan, which caps maximum processor state well below the CPU's rated boost speed. This is a configuration choice, not a hardware problem.
recommendation: Switch to the Balanced or High Performance power plan, or check 'Maximum processor state' under advanced power settings if it's capped below 100%.

goal: Random CPU spikes cause stutter in games even on a powerful CPU
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 Name, CPU

summary: A background telemetry/update-check process was spiking periodically and stealing CPU time slices from the game, causing the stutter -- not a GPU or game-engine issue.
recommendation: Disable or delay unnecessary background telemetry/updater tasks via Task Scheduler while gaming.

goal: PC suddenly shuts off completely during heavy load, like a game or render
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: The system has rebooted without cleanly shutting down first (Kernel-Power, Event 41)

summary: Event ID 41 (Kernel-Power) confirms the system lost power abruptly rather than shutting down cleanly, consistent with a thermal or power-protection shutdown under heavy CPU load.
recommendation: Check CPU temperatures under load with a monitoring tool, clean/reapply cooling, and verify the PSU has enough headroom for the CPU's power draw.

goal: Performance feels inconsistent, like only some CPU cores are being used
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Core parking was configured to keep up to half the logical cores parked to save power, which throttles multi-threaded performance under the active power plan.
recommendation: Set 'Minimum processor state' and core-parking minimum to 100% under the power plan's processor power management settings if you want full multi-core performance.

goal: One old 32-bit app pins a single CPU core to 100% and makes the whole PC feel slow
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-Process OldApp -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, CPU, Id

summary: The legacy app is single-threaded and doesn't spread work across cores, so it maxes out one logical core (visible as ~12% total on an 8-core CPU) while that core-bound operation feels slow.
recommendation: Check for an updated, multi-threaded version of the app; setting its process priority to Below Normal can reduce its impact on the rest of the system.

goal: SearchIndexer.exe uses high CPU for a long time after copying a huge folder of files
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Windows Search is indexing the large batch of newly added files so they become searchable, which is expected one-time CPU use that will taper off once indexing catches up.
recommendation: If it never settles, exclude rarely-searched folders (like large media archives) from indexing under Indexing Options.

goal: CPU-heavy tasks got noticeably slower after a Windows feature update
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Virtualization-based Security (Credential Guard/HVCI) was enabled by the feature update, which adds a small but real CPU virtualization overhead to every process -- a known security trade-off, not a fault.
recommendation: If the overhead isn't acceptable for your workload, VBS can be turned off under Core Isolation settings, though this reduces protection against credential-theft malware.

goal: wmiprvse.exe periodically spikes CPU to 100% for a minute at a time
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: A monitoring or security tool was issuing frequent, heavy WMI queries, which spins up WmiPrvSE.exe hosts that briefly spike CPU while they run.
recommendation: Check installed monitoring/inventory agents for an overly frequent polling interval and increase it if configurable.

goal: Just having a browser open with a few tabs uses a surprising amount of CPU
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-Process chrome | Select-Object -First 5 Name, CPU, Id

summary: Several tabs are running heavy JavaScript (ads, auto-playing video, and on some sites cryptomining scripts) that individually don't look like much but add up across tabs.
recommendation: Use Chrome's built-in Task Manager (Shift+Esc) to identify the specific tab/extension responsible and close or disable it.

goal: CPU and disk both spike briefly every week at the same time for no obvious reason
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The weekly Scheduled Defrag/optimize task was running (it also does TRIM on SSDs, which is normal and beneficial), accounting for the periodic CPU/disk activity.
recommendation: This is expected maintenance; no action needed unless you want to reschedule it to an idle time via Optimize Drives.

goal: CPU-Z / Task Manager shows the CPU stuck at its lowest possible frequency all the time
plan: Diagnose the cpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The CPU is pinned near its minimum frequency regardless of load, most commonly caused by the active power plan's 'Maximum processor state' being capped low, or a laptop stuck in a battery-saver-like state even on AC power.
recommendation: Check Power Options > Change plan settings > Advanced > Processor power management > Maximum processor state, and set it to 100% for both On battery and Plugged in.

goal: GPU usage shows 100% in Task Manager even sitting idle on the desktop
plan: Diagnose the gpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-Counter '\GPU Engine(*)\Utilization Percentage' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty CounterSamples | Where-Object CookedValue -gt 50

summary: A background browser tab with hardware-accelerated video decode running (e.g., an autoplay video) was pinning the GPU's video-decode engine, which Task Manager rolls up into overall GPU usage.
recommendation: Close or pause background video tabs; if it persists with nothing obviously playing, disable hardware acceleration in the browser as a test.

goal: Games stutter noticeably even though both CPU and GPU usage show under 60%
plan: Diagnose the gpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Neither the CPU nor GPU is actually maxed out, which points away from a raw performance bottleneck and toward a driver-level frame-pacing issue -- the installed GPU driver is notably out of date.
recommendation: Update to the latest vendor GPU driver (clean install) and check the game's frame-rate cap/V-Sync settings, which commonly cause this exact symptom.

goal: The GPU fan doesn't spin at all even under heavy gaming load
plan: Diagnose the gpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout:
Name                    Status
----                    ------
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 OK

summary: Windows reports the GPU itself as healthy, but modern GPUs use a 'zero RPM' fan mode that keeps fans off below a temperature threshold -- normal unless the card is also thermal throttling.
recommendation: Check the actual GPU temperature in the vendor's control panel (GeForce Experience/Adrenalin); fans should spin up once it crosses roughly 50-60C. If they never spin even when hot, that's a hardware fault worth servicing.

goal: Getting repeated 'Display driver stopped responding and has recovered' errors
plan: Diagnose the gpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: 3 TDR events logged in the last 24 hours, all referencing the same GPU driver

summary: Repeated TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) events confirm the GPU driver is timing out and being reset by Windows, typically from an unstable/overclocked GPU, an outdated driver, or insufficient power delivery.
recommendation: Reset any GPU overclock to stock, do a clean driver reinstall with DDU, and confirm the PSU meets the card's rated wattage.

recommendation: Go to Settings > System > Display > Graphics, add the game's .exe, and set it to 'High performance' to force the dedicated GPU.

recommendation: Clean reinstall the driver with DDU in Safe Mode; if Code 43 persists on a fresh driver and default clocks, the card itself may be failing and should be tested in another system.

recommendation: Check Thunderbolt security settings (set to 'No Security' or approve the device once), and connect/power on the eGPU before waking or booting the laptop.

goal: Video editing software crashes with an out-of-memory-style error during exports

recommendation: Lower the export/preview resolution or proxy settings, close other GPU-heavy apps during export, or consider a GPU with more VRAM for these project sizes.

recommendation: If you need full performance unplugged, check the vendor's GPU control panel for an option to disable battery-power throttling, understanding it will drain the battery much faster.

goal: GPU driver installer fails or rolls back every time partway through
plan: Diagnose the gpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

summary: Remnants of a previous GPU driver installation were conflicting with the new install, causing it to fail partway through and roll back.
recommendation: Fully remove the existing driver with Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) in Safe Mode, reboot, then install the new driver on a clean slate.

goal: GPU usage sits at 0-20% during gameplay while CPU is at 100%, framerate is still bad
plan: Diagnose the gpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The CPU is fully saturated while the GPU is mostly idle, meaning the CPU is the actual bottleneck for this game/settings combo -- more GPU power wouldn't help here.
recommendation: Lower CPU-bound settings (draw distance, NPC/physics density, background apps) rather than upgrading the GPU; closing background CPU-heavy apps often helps immediately.

goal: GPU fans spin up and usage stays high even when no games or apps are open
plan: Diagnose the gpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 Name, Id

summary: An unrecognized process with a name mimicking a system process was found driving GPU load with nothing else open -- consistent with unauthorized cryptomining/malware, not a legitimate app.
recommendation: Do not assume it's safe. Run a full Microsoft Defender offline scan immediately and remove the process/startup entry if confirmed malicious; consider a second-opinion scan from another reputable tool.

goal: A newly installed GPU performs far below its expected benchmarks
plan: Diagnose the gpu issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The GPU is correctly detected and healthy at the OS level; underperformance versus expected benchmarks is most commonly caused by the card negotiating a lower PCIe link speed/width (e.g., x4 instead of x16) rather than a driver or Windows issue.
recommendation: Check the PCIe slot and link speed/width reported in the vendor's GPU utility (e.g., GPU-Z); reseat the card fully in a full x16 slot and ensure the slot isn't bandwidth-limited by another installed device.

goal: PC won't boot, stops with a blue screen saying INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE
plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Kernel-Power Event 41 logged just before a bugcheck 0x0000007B was recorded

summary: Bugcheck 0x7B (INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE) indicates Windows lost access to the boot volume at startup, most often after a storage controller mode change (AHCI/RAID/NVMe) in BIOS or a failed storage driver update.
recommendation: Boot into Recovery > Advanced options > Command Prompt and run 'bootrec /fixboot' and 'bootrec /rebuildbcd'; if it started after a BIOS change, revert the SATA/NVMe mode back to what Windows was installed under.

goal: PC boots straight into 'Automatic Repair' every time and loops back to it
plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Boot critical file c:\windows\system32\drivers\stornvme.sys is corrupt

summary: SrtTrail.txt from the recovery log pointed to a corrupt boot-critical driver file, causing Automatic Repair to fail and loop instead of completing.
recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt, run 'sfc /scannow' targeting the offline OS or 'DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'; if that fails, disable automatic repair temporarily with 'bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No' to boot and investigate further.

goal: Getting 'The Boot Configuration Data file is missing some required information'
plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: The boot configuration data store could not be opened. The system cannot find the file specified.

summary: The BCD store itself is missing or corrupted, so Windows can't find valid boot entries to load from.
recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt run 'bootrec /rebuildbcd'; if it finds no Windows installations, rebuild manually with 'bcdboot C:\Windows'.

goal: Boot error: 'winload.efi is missing or contains errors'
plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The boot loader file winload.efi is missing from the System32 folder, which UEFI needs to hand off into Windows -- the BCD entry can't complete the boot chain.
recommendation: Rebuild the boot files from Recovery > Command Prompt with 'bootrec /rebuildbcd' followed by 'bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI' (where S: is the EFI system partition).

goal: PC won't boot after enabling Secure Boot, error about an untrusted boot loader
plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Secure Boot is active and rejecting the current boot loader/driver signature (common right after a dual-boot Linux install or an unsigned driver) -- the protection is working as designed rather than a fault.
recommendation: Either re-enable a Microsoft-signed boot path (repair Windows Boot Manager) or, if you intentionally need unsigned boot components, disable Secure Boot in BIOS/UEFI.

goal: 'Missing operating system' error on a BIOS/legacy boot drive
plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The Master Boot Record on the boot drive was damaged or overwritten, so the BIOS couldn't hand off to Windows. Rewriting a fresh, standard MBR is a safe first fix.
recommendation: Follow with 'bootrec /fixboot' and 'bootrec /rebuildbcd'; if a dual-boot loader (GRUB) was overwritten, you'll need to restore it separately.

goal: Disk shows as a GPT Protective Partition and Windows won't boot from it
plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The disk's GPT partition table header is unreadable (reporting RAW instead of GPT), which prevents the firmware from locating the EFI/boot partitions.
recommendation: This needs partition-table-level recovery (e.g., a read-only scan with a tool like TestDisk to rebuild the GPT) before the disk is bootable again; back up data first if any read access is still possible.

goal: 'No bootable device found' and the EFI system partition seems to be gone
plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: No partition with a GptType matching the EFI System Partition GUID was found

summary: The EFI System Partition (which holds the Windows Boot Manager) is missing from the partition table, so firmware has nothing to hand off to.
recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt, create a new FAT32 EFI partition with diskpart and run 'bcdboot C:\Windows /s <EFI drive letter> /f UEFI' to repopulate it.

goal: SSD randomly disconnects and reappears, sometimes with a different drive letter
plan: Diagnose the storage issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout:
FriendlyName    HealthStatus OperationalStatus
------------    ------------ -----------------
Samsung 970 EVO Unknown      Intermittent

summary: The SSD's operational status shows 'Intermittent' with an Unknown health read, a pattern typical of outdated/buggy SSD firmware causing the drive to drop off the bus under load.
recommendation: Check the manufacturer's tool (e.g., Samsung Magician) for a firmware update for this exact model; back up data first since firmware updates carry inherent risk.

goal: Getting a SMART warning about imminent drive failure
plan: Diagnose the storage issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The drive's SMART health status is reporting Warning, meaning its own self-monitoring has flagged degrading attributes (commonly reallocated or pending sectors) ahead of failure.
recommendation: Back up all data from this drive immediately and plan to replace it -- a SMART warning is a hardware early-warning sign, not something a software fix resolves.

goal: Newly installed NVMe SSD isn't detected anywhere in Windows
plan: Diagnose the storage issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: No NVMe device is enumerated at all, which points to it not being seated correctly, an M.2 slot conflict (shared PCIe lanes with SATA ports), or it not being enabled in BIOS, rather than a Windows issue.
recommendation: Reseat the NVMe drive, confirm the specific M.2 slot supports NVMe (not SATA-only) in the motherboard manual, and check BIOS for the slot being enabled.

goal: A secondary internal drive shows as 'BitLocker locked' and won't open
plan: Diagnose the storage issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The drive is fully BitLocker-encrypted and currently locked; without the password or recovery key, Windows correctly refuses access to protect the data.
recommendation: Unlock it with 'manage-bde -unlock D: -RecoveryPassword <48-digit-key>' using the recovery key saved to your Microsoft account, a USB key, or a printed copy.

goal: Can't write or delete anything on a drive, everything says read-only
plan: Diagnose the storage issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The disk itself is flagged read-only at the Windows disk-attribute level, often set automatically after certain BitLocker/diskpart operations or by a physical write-protect switch on some external drives.
recommendation: In an elevated prompt run 'diskpart', 'select disk 1', then 'attributes disk clear readonly'; check for a physical write-protect switch if it's an SD card or USB drive.

goal: Disk Management shows 'unallocated' on a drive that used to have data and partitions
plan: Diagnose the storage issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Get-Partition : No matching MSFT_Partition objects found

summary: No partitions are visible on the disk anymore, consistent with a corrupted partition table rather than the data itself being erased -- the raw data is often still physically present.
recommendation: Do not initialize or format the disk. Use a read-only partition-recovery tool (e.g., TestDisk) to attempt to rebuild the partition table before any write operations.

goal: Disk Management shows a dynamic disk as 'Foreign' or 'Missing'
plan: Diagnose the storage issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The dynamic disk's metadata isn't recognized by this system (commonly after moving it from another PC or a failed mirror/spanned volume), so Windows marks it Foreign instead of mounting it normally.
recommendation: In Disk Management, right-click the disk and choose 'Import Foreign Disks' -- only do this after confirming a current backup, as importing can affect volume sets that spanned multiple disks.

goal: After cloning a drive, only one of the two identical disks shows up correctly
plan: Diagnose the storage issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Both disks share the same on-disk signature because one is a raw clone of the other, so Windows treats the second as a duplicate/offline disk to avoid a conflict rather than mounting it normally.
recommendation: In Disk Management, bring the second disk online and let Windows prompt to write a new signature (this only touches the disk signature, not your data).

goal: Windows Memory Diagnostic reports errors after running the test
plan: Diagnose the memory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: The Windows Memory Diagnostic tested the computer's memory and detected hardware errors.

summary: The built-in memory diagnostic confirmed hardware-level RAM errors, which explains crashes/instability and is not something Windows can fix in software.
recommendation: Run MemTest86 overnight to identify which specific stick/slot is failing, then reseat or replace that module; if only one stick is installed, test it in a different slot to rule out a bad slot.

goal: PC won't boot (no display, beep codes) after adding a new RAM stick
plan: Diagnose the memory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_PhysicalMemory | Select-Object Manufacturer, Speed, Capacity
steps.stdout: (unreachable -- system fails to POST with the new module installed)

summary: The system fails to POST with the new module installed, a classic sign of a RAM compatibility issue (mismatched speed/timings/voltage or an unsupported module) rather than a Windows-level problem.
recommendation: Remove the new stick and confirm the PC boots on the original RAM alone; check the motherboard's QVL (Qualified Vendor List) before buying RAM, and try the new stick alone in slot 1 to isolate it.

goal: PC randomly blue-screens or crashes only since enabling XMP for faster RAM speed
plan: Diagnose the memory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The RAM is running above its rated 3200 MHz at the XMP-configured 3600 MHz, and instability appeared right after enabling that profile -- a strong sign the memory controller or kit can't hold the higher speed stably.
recommendation: Disable XMP (or step down to a slightly lower XMP speed) and retest stability; if you want to keep the higher speed, loosen the timings slightly or add a touch of DRAM voltage within the module's rated spec.

goal: Getting stop errors mentioning pagefile.sys, or the system won't hibernate
plan: Diagnose the memory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_PageFileUsage | Select-Object Name, AllocatedBaseSize, CurrentUsage

summary: The pagefile is showing a 0 MB allocated size, meaning virtual memory management has effectively been disabled or the file itself is misconfigured, which causes low-memory stop errors under load.
recommendation: Go to System Properties > Advanced > Performance Settings > Advanced > Virtual Memory and set it back to 'Automatically manage paging file size for all drives', then reboot.

goal: Getting 'Your computer is low on memory' warnings even though Task Manager shows RAM isn't maxed
plan: Diagnose the memory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_PageFileUsage | Select-Object AllocatedBaseSize, CurrentUsage, PeakUsage

summary: The pagefile (virtual memory) is nearly maxed out even though physical RAM has headroom, because the pagefile's fixed size is too small for the current workload's committed memory.
recommendation: Increase the pagefile size (or switch back to 'Automatically manage paging file size') under System Properties > Advanced > Performance > Virtual Memory, and close any single app with runaway memory commitment.

goal: Print Spooler service keeps crashing and needs constant restarting
plan: Diagnose the printer issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Faulting application spoolsv.exe, faulting module hpzcda01.dll

summary: A specific third-party printer driver DLL was crashing the spooler process itself, which is why restarting the service only provides a temporary fix.
recommendation: Update or reinstall the specific printer driver referenced in the crash; as a temporary workaround, remove that printer and re-add it using Windows' generic/basic driver.

goal: Print jobs come out garbled or in the wrong format after a driver update
plan: Diagnose the printer issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The installed driver version doesn't match the printer's actual firmware/language generation (e.g., a PCL6 driver against a PostScript-only printer), producing garbled output rather than a connectivity problem.
recommendation: Remove the current driver and install the exact model-specific driver from the manufacturer's site rather than a generic/similar-model driver.

goal: USB printer isn't detected even though it's powered on and cabled in
plan: Diagnose the printer issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: No printer device is enumerated over USB at all, which points to the cable/port or the USB Print driver stack rather than the printer's own configuration.
recommendation: Try a different USB cable and port (preferably directly on the PC, not through a hub); if still undetected, check Device Manager for an 'Unknown Device' entry, which would confirm a cable/port issue rather than a driver one.

goal: A printer shared from another PC on the network shows as offline
plan: Diagnose the printer issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The printer is shared from another computer, and that host PC is either asleep, off, or not sharing it currently -- the client-side printer object is healthy but has nothing to talk to.
recommendation: Wake/turn on the host PC and confirm printer sharing is still enabled there; consider connecting this printer directly to the network instead of relying on a host PC being awake.

goal: Print jobs to a network printer just time out and never print
plan: Diagnose the printer issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The PC can't reach the printer's network port (9100, the standard raw printing port) at all, which points to a network/IP issue -- the printer likely changed IP address rather than a driver problem.
recommendation: Confirm the printer's current IP address on its own control panel and update the port in Windows (or better, assign the printer a DHCP reservation/static IP so this doesn't happen again).

goal: Getting 'The trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain failed'
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout:
WARNING: The computer secure channel with domain CORP is not valid.
False

summary: The machine's secure channel password (stored locally and in AD) is out of sync with the domain controller, breaking the trust relationship used for authentication.
recommendation: Run 'Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair -Credential (domain admin)' to resync it without rejoining, or rejoin the domain if the repair fails.

goal: Domain logons fail intermittently with secure channel errors in the System log
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: 3 NETLOGON events indicating secure channel setup failures with DC02

summary: NETLOGON secure channel setup failures against a specific domain controller point to that DC being unreachable or having a replication issue, rather than a fault on this workstation.
recommendation: Confirm the affected DC is reachable and healthy ('nltest /dsgetdc:corp.local'); if one DC is the culprit, investigate replication issues on that DC separately.

goal: A user account keeps getting locked out repeatedly
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-ADUser jdoe -Properties LockedOut, BadLogonCount | Select-Object LockedOut, BadLogonCount

summary: The account is being locked out by repeated bad password attempts, most often from a stale cached credential on a phone/mapped drive/service retrying automatically rather than mistyping.
recommendation: Unlock the account, then check for saved credentials in Credential Manager, mapped drives, and mobile mail apps using the old password, and update them.

goal: Getting Kerberos errors (clock skew) trying to access domain resources
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: local clock is 00:07:14 ahead of dc01.corp.local

summary: The workstation's clock has drifted more than Kerberos's default 5-minute skew tolerance from the domain controller, so tickets are being rejected outright.
recommendation: Resync time against the domain with 'w32tm /resync /rediscover' and confirm W32Time is syncing from the domain hierarchy, not a local/external source.

goal: A newly created Group Policy hasn't applied on some computers days later
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Shows replication failures between two domain controllers with a non-zero fail count

summary: Active Directory replication between domain controllers is failing, so the new GPO exists on the DC where it was created but hasn't propagated to the DCs other sites authenticate against.
recommendation: Investigate the specific replication failure with 'repadmin /showrepl' on the affected DCs (commonly a DNS or connectivity issue between sites) rather than troubleshooting the GPO itself.

goal: IIS won't start, error says the port is already in use
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Another process is already bound to port 80, so IIS's site can't start on that port.
recommendation: Identify the conflicting service ('netsh http show servicestate'), stop it if unneeded (common culprits: Skype, another web server, or a previously running IIS site with an overlapping binding), then restart IIS.

goal: An IIS application pool keeps stopping itself shortly after starting
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Application pool 'DefaultAppPool' has been automatically disabled due to a series of failures

summary: IIS's rapid-fail protection automatically disabled the app pool after repeated worker process crashes within a short window, a symptom of an unhandled exception in the hosted app, not an IIS bug.
recommendation: Check the application's own event log/exception details for the root cause, then start the app pool again ('Start-WebAppPool -Name DefaultAppPool') once fixed.

goal: Site shows a certificate expired warning in the browser
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The bound SSL certificate expired, which is exactly what's producing the browser warning -- the site and IIS binding are otherwise fine.
recommendation: Renew the certificate (or issue a new one) and rebind it to the site in IIS Manager under Bindings > https > Edit > select the new certificate.

goal: Site returns a generic 500 error with no detail shown
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Detailed errors are set to show only for local requests, so remote browsers just see a generic 500 while the real exception is hidden -- a visibility setting, not the fix itself.
recommendation: Temporarily set httpErrors errorMode to 'Detailed' (local troubleshooting only, never facing the internet) to see the real stack trace, then check the application's own logs.

goal: Site returns 503 Service Unavailable for everyone
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The application pool backing the site is stopped, which produces a blanket 503 for every visitor -- the site's files and bindings are otherwise untouched.
recommendation: Start the app pool with 'Start-WebAppPool -Name DefaultAppPool'; if it immediately stops again, check the Application event log for the crash reason (rapid-fail protection) before restarting again.

goal: Docker Desktop hangs on 'Starting...' and never finishes
plan: Diagnose the docker issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The underlying Docker service never came up, which is why the Desktop UI hangs waiting for it -- a service-level failure to investigate rather than a Desktop UI bug.
recommendation: Check 'C:\ProgramData\DockerDesktop\service.log' for the specific startup error, and try Docker Desktop's built-in 'Troubleshoot > Clean / Purge data' as a reset option if the log doesn't point to an obvious fix.

goal: Docker Desktop shows 'WSL 2 installation is incomplete'
plan: Diagnose the docker issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout:
Default Distribution: docker-desktop
Default Version: 2
WSL 2 kernel file is not found

summary: The WSL2 Linux kernel component itself is missing, which Docker Desktop's WSL2 backend depends on entirely -- a Windows/WSL configuration gap, not a Docker-specific bug.
recommendation: Run 'wsl --update' to install/update the WSL2 kernel, then restart Docker Desktop.

goal: docker pull commands time out or fail with a network error
plan: Diagnose the docker issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The Docker engine can't reach Docker Hub's registry endpoint over HTTPS at all, pointing to a network/proxy/firewall block rather than a Docker configuration problem.
recommendation: If you're behind a corporate proxy, configure Docker Desktop's proxy settings under Settings > Resources > Proxies; otherwise check firewall rules for outbound 443 to registry-1.docker.io.

goal: A bind-mounted folder inside a container appears empty even though it has files on the host
plan: Diagnose the docker issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Mount source path is outside the drives enabled for file sharing in Docker Desktop

summary: The host path being mounted isn't enabled under Docker Desktop's file-sharing permissions, so the container sees an empty directory instead of an error.
recommendation: Add the drive/folder under Docker Desktop > Settings > Resources > File Sharing, then restart the container.

goal: A Hyper-V VM fails to start with a generic error
plan: Diagnose the hyperv issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Hyper-V reports no problem with the VM configuration; a VM that reports healthy status but still fails to start typically points to a resource conflict (not enough free RAM, or a locked virtual disk file).
recommendation: Check 'Get-VMMemory -VMName TestVM' against currently available host RAM, and confirm the VM's VHDX isn't still attached/locked by another process or a stale checkpoint.

goal: A VM lost network connectivity after a host reboot, virtual switch is gone
plan: Diagnose the hyperv issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: No virtual switches exist on the host anymore, which usually happens after a host network adapter was renamed/replaced (e.g., a driver update) and the switch's bound adapter no longer matches.
recommendation: Recreate the virtual switch with 'New-VMSwitch' bound to the current physical adapter name, then reattach it to the VM's network adapter.

goal: A VM won't start after trying to apply an old checkpoint
plan: Diagnose the hyperv issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Checkpoint chain shows a gap referencing a missing .avhdx file

summary: The checkpoint's differencing disk (.avhdx) file is missing or broken in the checkpoint chain, so Hyper-V can't reconstruct the VM's disk state at that point.
recommendation: Try applying a different (earlier or later) checkpoint that isn't broken; if none work, restore the VM's base VHDX from backup, as a broken checkpoint chain generally isn't repairable in place.

goal: A VM feels sluggish and can't use enhanced session mode / dynamic memory properly
plan: Diagnose the hyperv issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The VM's Hyper-V Integration Services are outdated relative to the host, which limits features like dynamic memory, time sync, and enhanced session mode and can cause sluggish behavior.
recommendation: Inside the guest OS, run Windows Update (integration services now ship via Windows Update on modern guests) to bring them current, then restart the VM.

goal: Outlook won't open, or opens with missing/duplicated emails
plan: Diagnose the office issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The local OST cache file (Outlook's offline copy of the mailbox) has become corrupted, which is why Outlook fails or shows inconsistent mail even though the actual mailbox on the server is fine.
recommendation: Close Outlook, run the built-in 'ScanPST.exe' repair tool against the .ost, or simply rename/delete the .ost (Outlook rebuilds it from the server for an Exchange/M365 account -- no data loss for server-hosted mail).

goal: Outlook can't automatically configure a new mailbox, autodiscover fails
plan: Diagnose the office issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The Autodiscover endpoint used to auto-configure the mailbox isn't reachable, so Outlook can't retrieve server settings automatically -- a DNS or network issue for that specific hostname.
recommendation: Verify the autodiscover DNS record with your mail admin/IT, and as a workaround, configure the account manually using the exact server settings provided by the mail admin.

goal: Excel crashes or hangs every time it starts, but only since installing a new add-in
plan: Diagnose the office issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The add-in is configured to load automatically at Excel startup, and it's crashing during that initialization, taking Excel down with it before the UI even appears.
recommendation: Start Excel in Safe Mode ('excel /safe') to confirm the add-in is the cause, then disable it from File > Options > Add-ins > COM Add-ins, and check for an updated version of the add-in.

goal: Word keeps opening in Safe Mode automatically and some features are missing
plan: Diagnose the office issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: (previous Word session was force-closed, tripping the safe-mode detector)

summary: Word detected that its previous session crashed or was force-closed, and starts in Safe Mode (add-ins/templates disabled) as a protective measure until confirmed stable.
recommendation: Close Word completely, then reopen it normally -- it usually exits Safe Mode after a clean start. If it keeps recurring, a corrupted Normal.dotm template is a common cause; renaming it forces Word to rebuild a fresh default.

goal: Microsoft Teams won't sign in, spins forever or errors out
plan: Diagnose the office issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Network connectivity to Teams' servers is fine, so the sign-in failure points to a corrupted local Teams cache/credential state rather than a connectivity problem.
recommendation: Fully quit Teams, clear its cache folder at '$env:AppData\Microsoft\Teams' (classic Teams) or reset the new Teams app via Settings > Apps, then sign in again.

goal: Windows Defender hasn't updated its virus definitions in weeks
plan: Diagnose the security issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Defender's signature database is over three weeks old, meaning it's not protecting against anything discovered since -- usually caused by the update task silently failing rather than Defender being disabled.
recommendation: Run 'Update-MpSignature' to force an immediate update; if it fails, check network access to Microsoft's update servers and that no policy is blocking signature updates.

goal: Certain older apps (some VPN clients, games) fail after enabling Credential Guard
plan: Diagnose the security issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Credential Guard is active and isolating credential material in a way that's incompatible with certain legacy authentication methods some apps rely on -- Credential Guard working as intended.
recommendation: Check with the specific app's vendor for Credential Guard compatibility; if it must be disabled for that one app, do so under Core Isolation settings, understanding the security trade-off.

goal: 'TPM device not detected' or Windows Hello/BitLocker won't set up
plan: Diagnose the security issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Windows doesn't see a usable TPM at all, which blocks any feature depending on it -- usually a BIOS setting rather than missing hardware on most modern systems.
recommendation: Enter BIOS/UEFI and enable the firmware TPM (often labeled 'fTPM', 'PTT', or 'Security Device Support' depending on the vendor), then re-check with 'Get-Tpm'.

goal: SmartScreen blocks a legitimate installer with 'Windows protected your PC'
plan: Diagnose the security issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: SmartScreen's reputation-based check flagged the installer because it lacks enough download reputation yet (common for new or unsigned installers), not necessarily because it's malicious.
recommendation: If you trust the exact source, click 'More info > Run anyway'; only do this for files from a source you fully trust, since this is also exactly what real malware relies on people doing.

goal: An app's firewall rule keeps getting silently removed or ignored
plan: Diagnose the security issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: A Group Policy-managed firewall policy is overriding the locally created rule, which is why it appears to keep 'disappearing' -- GPO firewall settings take precedence over local ones.
recommendation: The allow rule needs to be added via Group Policy (or the GPO needs to permit local rule merging) rather than locally on a domain-managed machine -- coordinate with IT/the policy owner.

goal: Some websites/apps fail intermittently, suspect IPv6 might be the problem
plan: Diagnose the network issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Resolves an IPv6 address but RemoteAddress is unreachable over IPv6; IPv4 succeeds separately

summary: The network prefers IPv6 for this destination but IPv6 routing/connectivity is broken (a common ISP/router misconfiguration), causing slow fallbacks or outright failures before IPv4 kicks in.
recommendation: As a diagnostic/workaround, disable IPv6 on the adapter to confirm it resolves the issue, then fix IPv6 routing at the router level rather than leaving it disabled long-term.

goal: Small requests work fine but larger file transfers or specific sites hang/fail
plan: Diagnose the network issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Packet needs to be fragmented but DF set.

summary: Packets above roughly 1472 bytes are being dropped rather than fragmented, indicating an MTU mismatch somewhere on the path (commonly a VPN or PPPoE connection with a smaller MTU than the adapter is configured for).
recommendation: Lower the adapter's MTU to match the path (often 1400-1454 for VPN/PPPoE) with 'netsh interface ipv4 set subinterface "Wi-Fi" mtu=1400 store=persistent', or enable Path MTU Discovery if it's disabled upstream.

goal: New devices on the network can't get an IP address, existing ones are fine
plan: Diagnose the network issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: New device shows an APIPA 169.254.x address instead of a DHCP-issued one

summary: New devices are falling back to APIPA, meaning DHCP requests aren't getting a response -- commonly because the DHCP server's address pool/scope is completely exhausted rather than a per-device fault.
recommendation: Check the DHCP server's scope for available addresses and either shorten the lease duration or expand the scope; also verify no rogue/second DHCP server is answering incorrectly.

goal: Getting 'Windows has detected an IP address conflict' pop-ups
plan: Diagnose the network issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: This machine has a static IP that falls inside the router's DHCP pool range, so the router occasionally hands the same address to another device, causing the conflict.
recommendation: Either move the static assignment outside the DHCP pool range, or better, set up a DHCP reservation for this device instead of a manual static IP.

goal: A device on a specific port can't reach anything even though the cable and switch port both test fine
plan: Diagnose the network issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Link is up at full speed, ruling out a cabling problem -- the switch port this device is connected to is very likely assigned to the wrong VLAN, putting it on a segment with no route to the resources it needs.
recommendation: Have the network admin confirm the switch port's VLAN assignment matches the VLAN this device is supposed to be on.

goal: Some apps can reach the internet but others (or the browser) can't
plan: Diagnose the network issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout:
Current WinHTTP proxy settings:

    Proxy Server(s) :  proxy.old-company.local:8080
    Bypass List     :  (none)

summary: A stale WinHTTP proxy (left over from a previous network/VPN configuration) is being used by apps that read the system-wide proxy setting, while apps with their own proxy setting are unaffected.
recommendation: Reset it with 'netsh winhttp reset proxy' if you no longer need a proxy, or point it at the correct current proxy server if one is still required.

goal: All network apps fail with generic connection errors after removing a VPN/antivirus product
plan: Diagnose the network issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The adapter is up and healthy, but the Winsock catalog was left corrupted after the VPN/antivirus's network filter driver was removed, breaking connections above the adapter level.
recommendation: Run 'netsh winsock reset' and reboot; this rebuilds the Winsock catalog to Windows defaults without affecting your files or other settings.

goal: Getting 'Registry corrupted' blue screens or Windows won't boot past the logo
plan: Diagnose the internals issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Windows was unable to load the registry hive SOFTWARE, it may be corrupt

summary: A core registry hive failed to load, which prevents Windows from completing boot since that hive holds essential configuration data.
recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt, restore the hive from its automatic backup copy under 'C:\Windows\System32\config\RegBack', or use System Restore to a point before the corruption occurred.

goal: Windows Update, feature installs, and DISM scans all fail with component store errors
plan: Diagnose the internals issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The WinSxS component store (which underlies servicing, updates, and optional feature installs) has detected repairable corruption, explaining the cascade of failures across multiple tools.
recommendation: Run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' to repair it using Windows Update as the source, then follow with 'sfc /scannow' for any remaining individual file issues.

goal: Need to find the actual cause behind repeated 'sfc /scannow' failures
plan: Diagnose the internals issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: [SR] Cannot repair member file [l:22]'oleaut32.dll' ... source could not be found

summary: The CBS.log pinpoints a specific file that SFC can't repair because it can't find a valid source copy on this system, explaining why repeated runs keep failing on the same component.
recommendation: Run 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' first to refresh the local component store (giving SFC a valid source to pull from), then re-run 'sfc /scannow'.

goal: Windows gets stuck applying updates every boot, 'Working on updates... Don't turn off your computer' never finishes
plan: Diagnose the internals issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: A stuck pending.xml file is tracking an update transaction that never completed, so Windows keeps trying (and failing) to finish the same servicing operation on every boot.
recommendation: This needs to be resolved carefully -- boot into Recovery, back up pending.xml, and follow Microsoft's guidance to clear the pending transaction; avoid deleting it outright without a backup.

goal: Can't install updates or modify certain system files, 'access denied' even as Administrator
plan: Diagnose the internals issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: TrustedInstaller (Windows Modules Installer), which owns many protected system files and update operations, isn't running -- many servicing operations legitimately fail without it.
recommendation: Set it back to Manual/Automatic startup with 'Set-Service TrustedInstaller -StartupType Manual' and start it; if the service is missing entirely, an in-place upgrade repair install may be needed.

goal: Clock resets to a wrong date every time the PC is unplugged, and BIOS settings don't stick
plan: Diagnose the hardware issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: (clock shows a date far in the past right after a cold boot with power disconnected)

summary: The CMOS battery that keeps BIOS settings and the clock alive while unpowered has died, so both reset every time the system loses main power completely.
recommendation: Replace the CR2032 CMOS battery on the motherboard (a $2-3 part), then re-enter any custom BIOS settings and let Windows resync the clock.

goal: PC won't POST/boot after a failed BIOS update
plan: Diagnose the hardware issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The system fails before POST completes, which is outside what Windows or PowerShell can diagnose -- this points to a corrupted/incomplete BIOS flash rather than a Windows or storage problem.
recommendation: Check the motherboard manual for a BIOS recovery procedure (many boards support a USB BIOS flashback or dual-BIOS failover); as a last resort, some boards need CMOS cleared via the jumper/battery-pull method.

goal: System randomly shuts down under load and a fan sounds like it's not spinning anymore
plan: Diagnose the hardware issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Kernel-Power Event 41 (unexpected shutdown, no clean shutdown recorded)

summary: The abrupt shutdown pattern combined with a fan that's stopped spinning strongly suggests a thermal-protection shutdown from inadequate cooling, rather than a software or power-supply fault.
recommendation: Physically inspect and, if needed, replace the stalled fan (CPU or case) before running the system under load again to avoid heat damage.

goal: All USB ports on one side of the PC stopped working simultaneously
plan: Diagnose the hardware issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.stdout: Several entries showing Status: Error, all sharing the same parent USB Host Controller

summary: Multiple devices under the same USB host controller are all in an Error state simultaneously, pointing to that specific controller failing rather than each individual device.
recommendation: Try the affected devices in ports on the other USB controller/side of the PC to confirm; if isolated to one controller consistently, try a driver reinstall first, then hardware service if that doesn't resolve it.

goal: A PCIe card that worked before is now gone from Device Manager entirely
plan: Diagnose the hardware issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

summary: The card isn't enumerating on the PCIe bus at all anymore (not even as an error device), which usually points to a seating/slot issue or a dead card rather than a driver problem.

recommendation: Create/edit '%UserProfile%\.wslconfig' with a '[wsl2] memory=4GB' cap, then run 'wsl --shutdown' to apply it on next launch.

recommendation: Run 'wsl --shutdown' and relaunch the distro to force WSL2 to rebuild its network adapter and refresh the localhost forwarding mapping.

goal: Users report their password changes on-premises aren't reflected in Microsoft 365 for hours
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this azuread issue

Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Azure AD Connect's sync scheduler had its interval changed to a much longer window than the default, so password/attribute changes are batching up for hours before syncing to Azure AD -- this is a scheduler configuration change, not a sync failure.
recommendation: Reset the sync interval back to the default with 'Set-ADSyncScheduler -CustomizedSyncCycleInterval 00:30:00', or trigger an immediate delta sync manually with 'Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta' when an urgent change needs to propagate.

goal: A Windows Failover Cluster keeps losing quorum and taking resources offline randomly
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this cluster issue
Identify the true root cause among several plausible candidates

summary: The cluster's file-share witness lives on a server that's been intermittently unreachable, and when both the witness and a node's network path degrade simultaneously the cluster loses majority vote and drops resources -- the cluster nodes themselves are healthy.
recommendation: Move the file-share witness to a highly available, independent server (or switch to a Cloud Witness if any node has internet access), and investigate the network path to the current witness server.

goal: A Cluster Shared Volume (CSV) drops into 'Redirected Access' mode, tanking storage performance
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this cluster issue

summary: A node lost direct storage connectivity (commonly a SAN/iSCSI path failure or lost cluster network), so the CSV coordinator redirected that volume's I/O over the cluster network to a node that still has direct access -- a resiliency feature working as designed, at a performance cost.
recommendation: Investigate and restore the affected node's direct storage path (check HBA/iSCSI initiator connections and multipathing), after which the CSV should automatically return to Direct I/O mode.

goal: Multiple internal web apps suddenly show certificate trust errors organization-wide

summary: The organization's internal Root Certificate Authority certificate itself expired, which breaks trust for every certificate it issued across every internal app simultaneously -- explaining the sudden, org-wide nature of the errors rather than individual app misconfigurations.
recommendation: This requires the PKI team to renew/reissue the Root CA certificate and redistribute it via Group Policy to all domain-joined machines' trusted root store; follow your organization's CA renewal runbook.

goal: A specific app can't validate a certificate, error mentions the CRL is unreachable
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this certificates issue
Identify the true root cause among several plausible candidates
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The certificate itself is valid, but the app can't reach the Certificate Revocation List (CRL) distribution point to confirm it hasn't been revoked, and strict validation settings are treating an unreachable CRL as a hard failure rather than a soft one.
recommendation: Restore network access to the CRL distribution point (cert.company.com), or if that's not possible, check whether the app/OS can be configured to fall back to OCSP or soft-fail on CRL unavailability.

goal: A scheduled task using a certificate for authentication stopped working after 'cleaning up' old certificates
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this certificates issue

summary: The certificate the scheduled task was pinned to by thumbprint was removed during the certificate cleanup, and because the task references a specific thumbprint rather than a subject name, it has nothing to fall back to -- a direct casualty of the cleanup rather than an unrelated fault.
recommendation: Reissue or restore a certificate with the expected properties, update the scheduled task's configuration with the new thumbprint, and going forward keep an inventory of which automation depends on which certificate before doing cleanup passes.

goal: Random BSODs with different bug check codes each time, no obvious single driver in common
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this bsod issue

steps.stdout: 3 distinct bug check codes (0x1E, 0x3B, 0x139) across the last 5 crashes

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_PhysicalMemory | Select-Object BankLabel, Capacity, ConfiguredClockSpeed

summary: Varying, unrelated bug check codes (rather than the same code every time) is a classic signature of unstable RAM rather than one bad driver -- especially with mismatched memory modules running at inconsistent clock speeds here.
recommendation: Run MemTest86 for at least a few passes to confirm; if errors show up, either match the RAM kit properly (same speed/timings/manufacturer) or run at the slowest common, stable speed.

goal: BSOD only happens during specific high-GPU-load moments, always the same bug check code
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this bsod issue
Identify the true root cause among several plausible candidates
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: A single, consistent bug check code tied directly to the GPU driver during high-load moments (unlike the RAM-instability pattern of varying codes) strongly points to the GPU driver itself as the specific fault, rather than a broader hardware stability issue.
recommendation: Update the GPU driver to the latest version via a clean install (DDU first), and if it's overclocked, return it to stock clocks since the crashes are load-triggered.

goal: WSUS console is extremely slow and some clients aren't reporting compliance status

steps.command: Invoke-Sqlcmd -ServerInstance 'localhost\SUSDB' -Query "SELECT COUNT(*) AS UpdateCount FROM tbUpdate"

summary: The WSUS database has accumulated far more approved/declined update revisions than recommended without ever being cleaned up, which degrades both console responsiveness and the SQL queries backing client compliance reporting -- a maintenance gap, not a service failure.
recommendation: Run the built-in WSUS Server Cleanup Wizard (or its PowerShell equivalent 'Invoke-WsusServerCleanup') to remove obsolete/superseded updates, and schedule it to run regularly going forward.

goal: Clients show 'downloading' at 0% forever when pulling updates from an internal WSUS server
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this wsus issue
Identify the true root cause among several plausible candidates
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Sum: far smaller than expected for the number of approved updates

summary: WSUS's metadata says updates are approved, but the actual update binary content was never fully downloaded to the WSUS content store, so clients connect fine but have nothing to actually download -- a content synchronization gap on the server, not a client-side issue.
recommendation: Run 'wsusutil.exe reset' on the WSUS server to force it to re-verify and re-download all approved update content from Microsoft, which can take a while depending on how much is missing.

goal: A DFS Namespace folder shows different (stale) content depending on which server a user's request lands on
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this dfs issue
Identify the true root cause among several plausible candidates
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: DFS Replication between the two servers backing this namespace has a large backlog, so users are seeing different content depending on which server's replica DFS happens to route them to until replication catches up.
recommendation: Check for what's blocking replication (commonly a recent large file change, a paused replication schedule, or a bandwidth-throttled connection between sites), and monitor with repeated 'Get-DfsrBacklog' calls until it drains.

goal: DFS Namespace referral sends users to a DFS server across a slow WAN link instead of their local one
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this dfs issue
Identify the true root cause among several plausible candidates
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The local site's DFS folder target is marked with a higher referral cost (or is offline) relative to the remote site's target, so Active Directory Site-aware referral is correctly routing users to the 'cheaper' remote target per its misconfigured cost value.
recommendation: Correct the referral ordering/cost for the local target under DFS Management, and confirm the local server's DFSR service is healthy if it's showing offline rather than just lower priority.

goal: A hardware RAID 5 array shows 'Degraded' status but all drives report as physically healthy in Windows
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this raid issue
Identify the true root cause among several plausible candidates
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Windows only sees the RAID controller's single logical volume, not the individual physical disks behind it, so 'all healthy' here just means the OS-visible volume is up -- the actual degraded/rebuilding state and any failed member disk needs to be checked in the RAID controller's own utility, not Windows Storage Management.
recommendation: Open the RAID controller's dedicated management tool (a vendor's Storage Manager/BIOS utility) to identify which physical member disk triggered the degraded state and whether a rebuild is in progress or a replacement disk is needed.

goal: Storage Spaces virtual disk shows 'Needs Repair' after a drive was briefly disconnected

------------ ------------ -----

summary: The brief disconnection left the storage pool's resiliency data (mirror/parity) out of sync across the physical disks; the disks themselves reconnected fine, but Storage Spaces flags the virtual disk for repair until it re-synchronizes the redundant copies.
recommendation: Run 'Repair-VirtualDisk -FriendlyName <name>' to trigger the resync; monitor progress with 'Get-StorageJob' until it completes, and avoid disconnecting drives from the pool while it's mid-repair.

goal: Multiple workstations show identical suspicious PowerShell activity in Sysmon logs around the same time
plan: Correlate multiple diagnostic signals for this security-incident issue
Identify the true root cause among several plausible candidates

steps.command: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational'; Id=1} -MaxEvents 20 | Where-Object Message -match 'powershell.exe' | Select-Object -First 3 TimeCreated
steps.stdout: 3 near-simultaneous PowerShell launches with -EncodedCommand across different hosts
Matching process-creation events with the same parent process across machines

summary: Coordinated, encoded PowerShell execution launching near-simultaneously across multiple hosts with a shared parent process is a strong indicator of lateral movement from a compromised management tool or credential, not isolated user activity -- this should be treated as an active incident.
recommendation: Escalate immediately per your incident response plan: isolate the affected hosts from the network, preserve the Sysmon/Security logs for forensics, and decode the captured -EncodedCommand payloads in an isolated analysis environment rather than on production hosts.

goal: An admin account shows sign-ins from two geographically distant locations within minutes

steps.stdout: Two 4624 logon events 6 minutes apart from IPs geolocating to different continents

summary: 'Impossible travel' between two sign-ins that are geographically infeasible within the observed time gap is a classic sign of credential compromise (the account is likely being used from two different actors/locations), not a single legitimate user traveling.
recommendation: Immediately force a password reset and revoke active sessions/tokens for this account, enable/require MFA if not already enforced, and review what that account accessed during the suspicious window as part of an incident investigation.

goal: A GPO applies to some computers in an OU but not others, no obvious pattern

summary: The GPO has a WMI filter scoped to a specific Windows build range, and the computers where it's 'not applying' are simply running a different OS build outside that filter's criteria -- targeted filtering working as designed, not a replication or application failure.
recommendation: If the WMI filter's OS version criteria is outdated (e.g., excluding newer builds it should now include), update the filter's WQL query to match the current intended scope.

goal: Users are unexpectedly getting local admin rights removed after each Group Policy refresh

summary: A Restricted Groups GPO is configured to authoritatively enforce the local Administrators group membership list, which silently strips out any manually added local admins on every policy refresh -- this is the GPO working exactly as configured, not a bug.
recommendation: If specific users legitimately need standing local admin rights, add them to the AD group referenced by the Restricted Groups policy itself rather than adding them locally, since local-only additions will keep being reverted.

goal: Health checks on a load balancer mark a healthy web server as 'down' periodically

recommendation: Increase the load balancer's health-check timeout/unhealthy-threshold slightly, or add a lightweight, separately-pooled health-check endpoint that isn't queued behind the application's regular request load.

goal: A file server feels slow under load; CPU, RAM, and disk queue length all look moderate individually

recommendation: Check the NIC's link speed/duplex settings for a mismatch, confirm it's not oversubscribed on a shared switch uplink, and consider NIC teaming or a faster adapter if legitimate throughput demand exceeds current capacity.

goal: Application response times spike every day at the same time, but server resource graphs look flat

recommendation: Reschedule the competing task to an off-peak window, or if it must run during business hours, throttle its I/O priority so it doesn't starve the foreground application.

goal: PC gets stuck in a boot loop, restarting itself over and over before reaching Windows

recommendation: Boot into Safe Mode (which loads a minimal driver set) to confirm it stays up; if Safe Mode is stable, use 'Get-WinEvent' on the System log from within Safe Mode to identify the last driver that loaded before each crash and roll it back.

goal: PC boots from the network (PXE) instead of the internal SSD every time

recommendation: Enter BIOS/UEFI setup and move the internal SSD/NVMe drive above Network Boot (PXE) in the Boot Order list, then save and exit.

goal: 'BOOTMGR is missing' error on a legacy BIOS system
plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks

summary: The Windows Boot Manager file itself is missing or unreadable from the active partition, so the BIOS has nothing to hand off to after POST.
recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt, also run 'bootrec /rebuildbcd' after fixboot; if the active partition flag was moved off the system partition, use diskpart to set it back with 'active'.

plan: Diagnose the boot issue with read-only checks

summary: WinRE's own partition/image was disabled or its boot entry pointed to a location that no longer exists, so Windows silently falls through instead of loading the recovery environment.
recommendation: Run 'reagentc /enable' from an elevated prompt in the working OS to re-register and re-enable the Recovery Environment.

goal: BitLocker keeps asking for the recovery key on every boot, even after entering it correctly each time
