summary: The correct recovery key unlocks the drive each time, but nothing is fixing the underlying protector -- the TPM protector was never re-added after being invalidated, so the same prompt recurs on every subsequent boot.
recommendation: After unlocking, run 'manage-bde -protectors -add C: -TPM' as admin to restore the TPM protector so future boots don't require manual entry.

goal: Startup Repair runs, reports it 'could not repair this PC', and offers no further detail

goal: Safe Mode is completely inaccessible, F8/Shift+Restart don't bring up the recovery menu

recommendation: Run 'bcdedit /set {default} bootmenupolicy legacy' to restore the classic F8 menu timing, or force the boot menu directly with 'shutdown /r /o /t 0' from a working session.

goal: Windows crashes to a blue screen every time right after installing a specific cumulative update

goal: Windows logo/spinning dots freeze permanently and the PC never reaches the lock screen

recommendation: Boot into Safe Mode and check Task Manager > Startup / Services for a third-party service that recently updated; disable it and boot normally to confirm, then reinstall/update that specific software.

recommendation: Let it run at least an hour past 100% before assuming it's stuck; if truly stalled, boot to Recovery and run 'DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions' to clear the stuck transaction, then retry the update.

plan: Diagnose the file issue with read-only checks

summary: Windows long-path support was disabled (LongPathsEnabled=0), so paths over 260 characters failed. Enabling it allows long paths for compliant apps.

summary: The Z: mapping to \\server\finance is connected, but the logged-in user (anita) lacks NTFS/share permissions on that folder, producing Access Denied.

plan: Diagnose the security issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: Several 4625 (failed logon) events occurred within seconds of each other overnight, consistent with an automated password-guessing attempt against the account.

summary: SmartScreen/PUA protection is on and flags the app because it lacks a known reputation (common for small or new publishers), not necessarily because it's malicious.

goal: Windows Search stopped working, typing in the box finds nothing
plan: Diagnose the windows issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The Windows Search service had stopped, so the index wasn't answering queries. Starting it restored search results.

goal: My printer shows offline even though it is on
plan: Diagnose the windows issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The spooler was running but in a stuck state, showing the printer offline. Restarting the Print Spooler cleared the stuck status and the printer returned to Normal.
recommendation: If it goes offline again, clear stuck jobs and uncheck 'Use Printer Offline'.

goal: My Start menu won't open when I click it
plan: Diagnose the windows issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The Explorer shell that hosts the Start menu had gotten into a bad state. Restarting explorer.exe rebuilt the shell and the Start menu opened again.
recommendation: If it recurs after updates, run 'sfc /scannow' to check shell components.

goal: The clock shows the wrong time and won't sync
plan: Diagnose the windows issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: The Windows Time service (W32Time) was stopped, so the clock drifted and couldn't sync. Starting the service and forcing a resync corrected the time.
recommendation: Ensure W32Time startup is Automatic (or 'Automatic (Delayed)') so it syncs at boot.

plan: Diagnose the windows issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-Service ClipSVC, wuauserv | Select-Object Name, Status

summary: The Client License Service (ClipSVC), which Store apps need to validate licenses, was stopped, so the apps failed to launch. Starting it let them open.
recommendation: If they still fail, run 'wsreset.exe' to clear the Store cache.

recommendation: Press Win+P and choose Extend, reseat the HDMI/DP cable and select the right input, then update the GPU driver.

goal: Windows Update keeps failing with an error code
plan: Diagnose the windows issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation

steps.command: Get-Service wuauserv, cryptSvc, bits, msiserver | Select-Object Name, Status

recommendation: Re-run Windows Update; if it still fails, clear SoftwareDistribution and retry.

goal: An old app looks blurry on my high-resolution screen
plan: Diagnose the windows issue with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate safe fix or give a clear recommendation
summary: On a high-DPI screen Windows scales the UI up, and the legacy app doesn't support DPI scaling, so Windows bitmap-stretches it and it looks blurry. This is an app limitation, not a display fault.
recommendation: Right-click the app's .exe > Properties > Compatibility > Change high DPI settings > 'Override' and pick 'System (Enhanced)'.

goal: Getting error 0x80070005 'Access is denied' when installing Windows updates
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Error 0x80070005 during updates means the update process lacked permission to write to a required folder or registry key, most often because security-software restrictions or broken ACLs on the SoftwareDistribution/Catroot2 folders are blocking TrustedInstaller.
recommendation: Run the update as the SYSTEM context does (no manual elevation fixes this): restore default ACLs with 'icacls C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution /reset /t', temporarily disable third-party antivirus, and retry.

goal: An app fails with error 0x80004005 'Unspecified error' when accessing a network share
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x80004005 is a catch-all failure, but paired with a network share it almost always maps to an SMB authentication/protocol negotiation failure -- here the client had insecure guest auth disabled while the share only allows guest access.
recommendation: The secure fix is enabling authenticated access on the share (add a real user account on the NAS/server); enabling insecure guest logons on the client works but reintroduces a security risk.

goal: Blue screen with stop code 0xC000021A (STATUS_SYSTEM_PROCESS_TERMINATED) after an update
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Bugcheck 0xc000021a recorded immediately after the last update attempt

summary: 0xC000021A means a critical user-mode subsystem process (winlogon/csrss) died, typically after a file mismatch introduced by an interrupted update or a third-party service DLL injected into the logon path.
recommendation: Boot to Recovery and run 'sfc /scannow /offbootdir=C:\ /offwindir=C:\Windows' followed by 'DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'; if a third-party credential/logon tool was recently installed, uninstall it from Safe Mode.

goal: Windows Update fails repeatedly with 0x80070490 'Element not found'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Windows Resource Protection found corrupt files and successfully repaired them.

summary: 0x80070490 indicates a corrupted entry in the component-based servicing (CBS) store or a damaged system file the update depends on -- the update engine literally can't find a manifest element it expects.
recommendation: Run DISM RestoreHealth then SFC (in that order), reboot, and retry the update; if it still fails, install the update manually from the Microsoft Update Catalog.

goal: MSI installer fails with error 1603 'A fatal error occurred during installation'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Return value 3. CustomAction InstallFiles returned actual error code 1603 -- Access denied writing to target folder

summary: Error 1603 is a generic MSI failure, and the verbose MSI log here shows the real cause: the installer tried writing to a folder redirected/locked by policy, so the transaction rolled back.
recommendation: Re-run with verbose logging ('msiexec /i app.msi /L*v log.txt') to confirm the failing action, clear the target folder's lock/permission problem, ensure no other MSI is in progress, and retry.

goal: Enabling .NET Framework 3.5 fails with error 0x800F081F 'source files could not be found'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x800F081F means the on-demand feature payload isn't in the local component store and Windows couldn't fetch it (commonly blocked by WSUS policy that redirects feature-on-demand requests away from Windows Update).
recommendation: Enable it with an explicit source from matching install media: 'DISM /Online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:NetFx3 /All /Source:D:\sources\sxs /LimitAccess', or have IT enable the 'Specify settings for optional component installation' GPO to allow direct Windows Update fetch.

goal: Windows 10 to 11 feature update fails with 0xC1900101 and rolls back
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: 0xC1900101 - 0x20017: driver migration failure referencing a third-party storage filter driver

summary: 0xC1900101 is a driver-related rollback code: setup's compatibility log shows a storage/AV filter driver failing migration, which aborts the upgrade and rolls back to the previous build every time.
recommendation: Update or temporarily uninstall the specific driver/security product named in setuperr.log, disconnect nonessential peripherals, and retry the feature update; reinstall the software afterward.

goal: Installing from a USB/ISO fails with error 0x80070570 'The file or directory is corrupted and unreadable'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: (hash mismatch versus the official published SHA256)

summary: 0x80070570 during install points to corrupted source media or failing RAM -- the installer read data that didn't match its checksums, and here the ISO's hash doesn't match Microsoft's published value.
recommendation: Re-download the ISO and re-create the USB with the official Media Creation Tool; if a verified-good USB still throws 0x80070570, run MemTest86 because failing RAM produces this same error.

goal: Windows Update error 0x8007000D 'The data is invalid' on every update attempt
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Get-Service wuauserv, bits, cryptsvc | Select-Object Name, Status
steps.stdout:
Name     Status
----     ------
wuauserv Running
bits     Running
cryptsvc Running

summary: 0x8007000D means the update datastore or a downloaded package is malformed -- the update engine is parsing invalid data, usually from a corrupted download cache rather than the update itself.
recommendation: Stop wuauserv/bits/cryptsvc, rename both 'SoftwareDistribution' and 'System32\catroot2', restart the services, and re-check for updates so everything re-downloads cleanly.

goal: Corporate PC shows update error 0x80244022 whenever checking for updates
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x80244022 (WU_E_PT_HTTP_STATUS_503) means the configured WSUS server responded 'Service Unavailable' -- the client-side is healthy and the update failure is entirely the WSUS server's IIS app pool being down.
recommendation: Report to IT: the WsusPool IIS application pool on the WSUS server needs restarting (and usually a private-memory limit increase to stop it recycling under load).

goal: An application crashes repeatedly with exception code 0xC0000005 (Access Violation)
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0xC0000005 is a memory access violation inside the app; the crash dumps consistently blame the same third-party DLL injected into the process (a shell/overlay hook), not the application's own code.
recommendation: Update or uninstall the software owning the faulting DLL (screen-overlay/RGB/antivirus injectors are common); if unclear, run the app with overlays disabled to confirm.

goal: Windows Update error 0x8024402C 'proxy or firewall configuration problem'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Proxy Server(s): 127.0.0.1:8888 (stale entry from removed software)

summary: 0x8024402C means the update client couldn't resolve/reach the update endpoints, and here a stale WinHTTP proxy (separate from the browser proxy) is black-holing the system-level HTTPS traffic.
recommendation: Run 'netsh winhttp reset proxy', confirm no manual proxy remains in Settings > Network > Proxy, then retry Windows Update.

goal: Blue screen DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE (0x9F) when sleeping or waking the laptop
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Two unexpected restarts, both immediately after sleep was initiated

summary: 0x9F means a driver failed to complete a power-state transition in time; the recorded blocked IRP points at the wireless adapter's driver hanging during suspend.
recommendation: Update the Wi-Fi adapter driver (the usual culprit for 0x9F on laptops), and as a stopgap disable 'Allow the computer to turn off this device' on that adapter so suspend doesn't hang on it.

goal: Blue screen CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED (0xEF) shortly after logging in
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0xEF fires when a process Windows marks as critical exits unexpectedly; correlating times shows svchost.exe hosting a critical service was being terminated by a third-party 'RAM optimizer' utility at each login.
recommendation: Uninstall the process-killing 'optimizer' utility -- terminating protected svchost processes directly causes CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED; also run 'sfc /scannow' to verify no system files were damaged.

goal: Blue screen PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA (0x50) at random moments
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x50 means the kernel referenced invalid memory in the nonpaged pool -- with crashes at random (not tied to one driver or action) and mismatched RAM speeds installed, unstable memory is the leading cause.
recommendation: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic/MemTest86; set both DIMMs to the same (lower) speed in BIOS or replace the mismatched kit with a matched pair.

goal: Error 0x80070002 'The system cannot find the file specified' during Windows backup or update
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: True (folder present but nearly empty despite pending updates)

summary: 0x80070002 means a file the operation's manifest references is missing on disk -- here update staging references files that were cleaned out of SoftwareDistribution mid-cycle by a disk-cleanup tool.
recommendation: Stop wuauserv, clear the SoftwareDistribution folder completely so tracking matches reality, restart the service, and re-scan; exclude that folder from aggressive cleanup tools going forward.

goal: Microsoft Store or activation fails with 0x80072F8F 'A security error occurred'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: local clock is 4 days, 02:11:08 behind server time

summary: 0x80072F8F is a TLS handshake failure, and the root cause here is the system clock being off by several days -- certificate validity checks fail when local time falls outside the cert's window.
recommendation: Start W32Time and resync ('Start-Service W32Time; w32tm /resync'); with a correct clock the TLS errors disappear. If the clock drifts again after shutdowns, replace the CMOS battery.

goal: Windows activation fails with 0x803FA067 after reinstalling Windows
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Get-CimInstance SoftwareLicensingProduct -Filter "PartialProductKey IS NOT NULL" | Select-Object Name, LicenseStatus

summary: 0x803FA067 means the digital license lookup didn't match: the machine was reinstalled with a different edition (Pro media over a Home digital license), so activation correctly refuses the mismatched edition.
recommendation: Either reinstall the edition matching the original digital license (Home), or purchase/enter a valid Pro key; the edition must match what the hardware's digital license was issued for.

goal: Volume-licensed office PC shows activation error 0xC004F074 'Key Management Service is unavailable'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0xC004F074 means no KMS host answered: the client's KMS SRV lookup succeeds but the KMS host itself is unreachable on port 1688 from this network segment.
recommendation: Report to IT that port 1688 to the KMS host is blocked from this subnet (or the KMS host is down); once reachable, activate immediately with 'slmgr /ato'.

goal: Service operations fail with 0x800706BA 'The RPC server is unavailable' against a remote machine
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x800706BA against a remote host means the RPC endpoint mapper (TCP 135) or the dynamic RPC ports are blocked -- the remote host is up but its firewall only permits ping, not RPC.
recommendation: Enable the 'Remote Service Management' / 'Windows Management Instrumentation' firewall rule groups on the remote host (or the equivalent GPO), which open TCP 135 plus the dynamic RPC range.

goal: Accessing a share fails with 0x80070035 'The network path was not found' though ping works
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x80070035 with successful ping means name resolution works but SMB (TCP 445) is unreachable -- the target machine has file sharing disabled or its firewall is blocking the File and Printer Sharing rule group.
recommendation: On the target machine, enable 'File and Printer Sharing' in the firewall for the correct network profile, and confirm the 'Server' (LanmanServer) service is running.

goal: Blue screen DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (0x133) mainly during heavy disk activity
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context

steps.stdout:
DeviceName                     DriverVersion
----------                     -------------
Standard SATA AHCI Controller  10.0.19041.1

summary: 0x133 means a deferred procedure call ran too long at high IRQL; on this machine it correlates with an SSD running legacy storage drivers, a classic combination for DPC watchdog timeouts under I/O load.
recommendation: Update the storage controller driver (vendor IRST/NVMe driver where applicable) and the SSD's firmware; both are the standard fixes for 0x133 tied to disk activity.

goal: Windows installation fails with 0x80300024 'Windows is unable to install to the selected location'

summary: 0x80300024 means setup can't use the chosen disk -- with multiple drives connected, setup put boot files on a different disk than the install target, creating a conflict.
recommendation: Temporarily disconnect all drives except the intended target, install Windows, then reconnect the other drives; this guarantees boot files land on the right disk.

goal: Store apps fail to update with error 0x80073CF9

summary: 0x80073CF9 is a package deployment failure, and here the AppX staging folder has broken ACLs after a profile migration, so packages can't be extracted during install/update.
recommendation: Reset the Store cache with 'wsreset.exe', then re-register the Store: 'Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.WindowsStore | Foreach {Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -Register "$($_.InstallLocation)\AppXManifest.xml"}'; check ACLs on 'C:\Program Files\WindowsApps' if it persists.

goal: Outlook/Microsoft 365 sign-in fails with error 0x80190001
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x80190001 is an HTTP failure during Azure AD token retrieval -- TLS inspection by a proxy is intercepting the authentication traffic, breaking certificate pinning for the Microsoft 365 endpoints.
recommendation: Have IT exclude Microsoft 365 authentication endpoints (login.microsoftonline.com and related URLs from Microsoft's published list) from TLS/SSL inspection on the proxy.

goal: SCCM/Intune app deployment fails on clients with error 0x87D00668

Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

summary: 0x87D00668 means the client received the deployment but the software change returned 'requirement not met' -- the deployment's requirement rule (minimum OS build) excludes these machines, so the agent correctly skips installation.
recommendation: Either update the targeted machines to the required OS build, or adjust the application's requirement rules in SCCM/Intune to include the older builds intentionally.

goal: Windows Hello for Business enrollment fails with 0x801C03ED
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x801C03ED means the device registration completed but the directory hasn't synced the device object yet -- enrollment is racing ahead of Azure AD Connect's sync cycle, so the server rejects the not-yet-visible device.
recommendation: Wait for (or trigger) an Azure AD Connect delta sync so the device object reaches Azure AD, then retry enrollment; recurring cases usually mean the sync interval is set too long.

goal: Remote Desktop fails with 'CredSSP encryption oracle remediation' error (0x800706BE variant)
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The client and server have mismatched CredSSP patch levels: one side enforces the hardened CredSSP protocol while the other is unpatched, so the connection is rejected by policy rather than a network fault.
recommendation: Patch the unpatched side (preferred) with current Windows updates; only as a temporary bridge, relax enforcement via the 'Encryption Oracle Remediation' GPO, and revert once both sides are patched.

goal: Windows Search/Outlook search broken, event log full of ESENT error 455 about a missing log file
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: ESENT 455 means a database engine log file was deleted while its database was still marked dirty -- a cleanup tool removed Windows.edb transaction logs, leaving the search index unable to recover.
recommendation: Stop WSearch, delete the search Data folder contents so the index rebuilds from scratch, restart the service, and exclude the search database path from cleanup tools.

goal: Scheduled task fails with 0x1 exit code but runs fine manually
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'NightlyExport' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Principal | Select-Object UserId, LogonType

summary: Exit code 0x1 from a scheduled task that works interactively almost always means an environment difference: the task runs as SYSTEM with no network drive mappings, and the script references a mapped drive letter only the interactive user has.
recommendation: Replace mapped drive letters with full UNC paths in the script, and set the task's 'Start in' directory explicitly; grant the run-as account NTFS access to the UNC target.

goal: Printing fails with error 0x0000011B on a shared network printer
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x0000011B stems from the PrintNightmare-era RPC authentication hardening: the print server enforces packet privacy while the client-side connection was established before the fix, so the mismatch rejects the job.
recommendation: Update both client and print server fully with current Windows updates, then remove and re-add the printer connection; avoid registry workarounds that disable RPC authentication hardening.

goal: Windows Backup (wbadmin) fails with 0x8078002A on a large external drive
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x8078002A occurs when block-level backup hits a target using 4K-native sectors that the backup engine can't handle -- the external drive reports 4096-byte logical sectors, which wbadmin's VHD format doesn't support.
recommendation: Use a 512-byte-emulation (512e) drive as the backup target, check the drive vendor's tool for a sector-emulation mode, or switch to File History/a third-party imaging tool that supports 4Kn targets.

goal: Domain join fails with error 0x6D9 'There are no more endpoints available from the endpoint mapper'

summary: 0x6D9 during domain join means the client reached the DC for the initial lookup but the follow-up RPC connection to the domain controller's dynamic ports was blocked by a firewall between them.
recommendation: Open the dynamic RPC port range (49152-65535 by default) between client and domain controllers on the intervening firewall, or configure a static RPC port range per Microsoft's guidance if broad ranges aren't allowed.

summary: 4720 on a workstation outside any provisioning window is a red flag: the event's Subject shows which account performed the creation, and here it was done by a local account at 3 AM -- consistent with persistence-building after a compromise.
recommendation: Treat as an incident: disable the created account, isolate the machine, review 4624/4672/4688 events around the same window to trace how the creating account was accessed, and reset its credentials.

goal: Volume reports MFT corruption -- files exist but some can't be opened and chkdsk finds MFT errors
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Errors found in the Master File Table (MFT)... 12 unreadable file record segments.

summary: The Master File Table has damaged records; chkdsk's read-only scan reports unreadable MFT segments, meaning metadata for some files is lost even though their data clusters may be intact.
recommendation: Back up everything readable first, then run 'chkdsk D: /f' to rebuild what's recoverable (files with destroyed records land in Found.000); recurring MFT damage on a healthy disk suggests a controller/cable issue corrupting writes.

goal: USN Journal corruption breaks backup/sync tools with 'The USN journal is invalid' errors
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Error: The journal entry has been deleted from the journal.

summary: The change journal that incremental tools rely on is damaged; tools that track changes via USN can't resume and error out rather than falling back to full scans automatically.
recommendation: Delete and recreate the journal: 'fsutil usn deletejournal /d D:' then 'fsutil usn createjournal m=32768000 a=4096000 D:'; affected tools will do one full rescan and then resume incremental tracking.

goal: A file shows 0 bytes in Explorer but takes real disk space -- data hidden in Alternate Data Streams
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The file's content lives in a named NTFS alternate data stream rather than the main stream, so Explorer shows zero size; ADS is legitimate NTFS functionality but also a classic data-hiding spot.
recommendation: Read the stream with 'Get-Content note.txt -Stream hidden' to inspect it; remove with 'Remove-Item note.txt -Stream hidden'. Audit unexpected ADS on user-writable paths -- malware droppers use them for staging.

goal: A backup tool loops forever on a folder tree -- a junction points back into its own parent
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Get-ChildItem C:\Data -Recurse -Attributes ReparsePoint -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object FullName, Target

summary: A directory junction inside the tree targets an ancestor folder, creating an infinite recursion loop for any tool that follows reparse points instead of detecting cycles.
recommendation: Remove the looping junction ('Remove-Item C:\Data\Archive\Loop' removes only the link, not the target), and configure backup tools to not follow reparse points, which also protects against future loops.

goal: Hard-linked files confuse disk usage tools -- deleting a 'copy' doesn't free space
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The files are hard links: multiple directory entries sharing one data extent, so space frees only when the last link is deleted -- usage tools double-count them and deletions of one name appear to 'do nothing'.
recommendation: This is expected NTFS behavior (used heavily by WinSxS); to actually reclaim space, all link names must be removed. Use tools that count hard links once when auditing usage.

goal: Disk quota exceeded errors for a user even though the volume has plenty of free space
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout:
Quota state: Enforced
User: CORP\jdoe  Limit: 10 GB  Used: 10.4 GB

summary: Per-user NTFS quotas are enforced on this volume, and the user's charged bytes (including files they own anywhere on the volume) exceed their limit -- overall free space is irrelevant to the quota check.
recommendation: Raise or remove the user's quota entry ('fsutil quota modify' or the volume's Quota tab), or have the user delete/transfer ownership of large files; quota charges follow file ownership, not folder location.

goal: ACL corruption -- Explorer's Security tab shows 'The permissions on ... are incorrectly ordered' errors
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: D:\Share\Projects: The ACL is not in canonical form.

summary: The security descriptor's ACEs are stored in non-canonical order (explicit denies must precede allows, etc.), typically after a nonconforming tool wrote the ACL directly -- Windows refuses edits until order is fixed.
recommendation: Fix with 'icacls D:\Share\Projects /reset /t' (rebuilds from inheritance) if inherited permissions suffice, or reorder in the Security tab's Advanced dialog by re-applying permissions; identify and stop the tool writing broken ACLs.

goal: SMB signing mismatch -- connecting to a hardened server fails with 'The cryptographic signature is invalid'
plan: Diagnose the smb issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The server now requires SMB signing per new policy, and this client has signing disabled via an old registry tweak, so the security negotiation fails outright rather than falling back.
recommendation: Re-enable client signing: 'Set-SmbClientConfiguration -EnableSecuritySignature $true' (and remove the legacy registry tweak that disabled it); signing adds minimal overhead on modern hardware.

goal: Offline Files (Client-Side Caching) shows stale content and won't sync back to the server
plan: Diagnose the smb issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The Offline Files cache database is stuck in a conflicted state; the sync center reports conflicts but the CSC cache itself is damaged, so resolution attempts loop without writing changes server-side.
recommendation: Save copies of locally changed files first, then reinitialize the CSC cache (set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CSC\Parameters\FormatDatabase=1 and reboot) -- this discards the cache and re-syncs cleanly from the server.

goal: Network discovery shows no computers in File Explorer's Network view though shares work by UNC path
plan: Diagnose the smb issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Discovery depends on the Function Discovery services and the network profile being Private; here the profile is Public (which disables discovery by design) after the last network change.
recommendation: Set the network to Private ('Set-NetConnectionProfile -Name HomeLAN -NetworkCategory Private') and ensure Function Discovery Resource Publication / FDPHost services run; UNC paths bypass discovery, which is why they still worked.

goal: Share permissions vs NTFS permissions mismatch -- user has Full Control on the share but still can't write
plan: Diagnose the smb issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Effective access over SMB is the most restrictive combination of share and NTFS permissions: the share grants Full Control but NTFS grants only Read, so writes fail despite the generous share ACL.
recommendation: Grant the group Modify at the NTFS level ('icacls D:\Shares\TeamDocs /grant "CORP\team-users:(OI)(CI)M"'); best practice is Everyone/Authenticated Users Full at the share layer and real control via NTFS.

goal: Two machines report SID-related trust errors after being cloned from the same image without sysprep
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: (identical UUID/SID lineage confirmed across both clones)

summary: Both clones share the same machine SID and, more critically, identical computer account credentials history -- domain trust and some security functions misbehave because the clones were never generalized with sysprep.
recommendation: Rebuild the clones properly: run 'sysprep /generalize' on the source image and redeploy; for the existing machines, disjoin, delete their AD computer objects, and rejoin after re-generalizing.

goal: Kerberos fails for one service with 'duplicate SPN' errors and intermittent authentication
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout:
Found 1 group of duplicate SPNs:
HTTP/intranet.corp.local registered on CORP\svc-web-old and CORP\svc-web

summary: The same ServicePrincipalName is registered on two different accounts, so the KDC issues tickets for whichever it finds first -- when it's the wrong account, the service can't decrypt the ticket and auth fails intermittently.
recommendation: Remove the SPN from the obsolete account ('setspn -D HTTP/intranet.corp.local svc-web-old'); duplicate SPNs must never coexist -- the intermittent pattern matches which object the KDC happened to resolve.

goal: Applications fail LDAP binds against the Global Catalog while normal LDAP (389) works
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The app queries the Global Catalog on port 3268, and the only local GC-enabled DC is offline -- regular LDAP on 389 still answers from a non-GC DC, which is why only GC-dependent lookups fail.
recommendation: Bring the GC DC back online or enable the GC role on another local DC (NTDS Settings > Global Catalog checkbox), then allow replication to complete; site designs should always include at least two GCs.

goal: A branch office Read-Only Domain Controller (RODC) can't authenticate some users when the WAN is down
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The RODC only caches passwords for accounts in its Password Replication Policy allow list; users outside it require a writable DC over the WAN, so they fail exactly when the WAN link is down.
recommendation: Add the branch users' group to the RODC's allowed Password Replication Policy and pre-populate their secrets ('repadmin /rodcpwdrepl'); only cached accounts survive WAN outages by design.

goal: Reverse DNS lookups fail (PTR records missing) breaking tools that resolve IPs to names
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Resolve-DnsName : DNS name does not exist

summary: The forward zone is healthy but no reverse lookup zone exists for the subnet, so PTR queries have nowhere to land -- reverse zones are never created automatically.
recommendation: Create the reverse zone (2.0.10.in-addr.arpa) on the DNS server, enable secure dynamic updates so clients register their own PTRs, and add static PTRs for servers/printers with static IPs.

goal: Stale DNS records accumulate -- offline machines still resolve because scavenging never runs
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Aging/scavenging is disabled on the zone, so dynamically registered records persist forever after machines are gone; lookups keep resolving to dead IPs.
recommendation: Enable aging on the zone and scavenging on the server ('Set-DnsServerZoneAging corp.local -Aging $true' plus Set-DnsServerScavenging with sensible no-refresh/refresh intervals matched to DHCP lease duration); verify timestamps before first scavenge so valid records aren't purged.

goal: Domain controller SRV records missing from DNS -- clients can't locate DCs after a DNS rebuild
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Resolve-DnsName : DNS name does not exist

summary: The _ldap/_kerberos SRV records under _msdcs were lost in the zone rebuild, and clients discover DCs exclusively through them -- without SRVs, domain operations fail even though A records exist.
recommendation: On each DC, restart the Netlogon service ('Restart-Service Netlogon') which re-registers all its SRV records automatically; verify with the same SRV query, and check the zone allows secure dynamic updates.

goal: Secondary DNS server's zone is stale -- zone transfers (AXFR/IXFR) are being refused
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The primary's zone-transfer settings don't include the new secondary's IP, so transfer requests are refused and the secondary keeps serving its aging copy until expiry.
recommendation: Add the new secondary's IP to the allowed transfer list ('Set-DnsServerPrimaryZone corp.local -SecondaryServers 10.0.1.10,10.0.1.11 -SecureSecondaries TransferToSecureServers') and trigger a transfer from the secondary.

goal: DNSSEC validation failures -- some external domains fail with SERVFAIL only through the internal resolver
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The internal resolver has DNSSEC validation enabled and its trust anchor for the root zone is outdated (missed the KSK rollover), so signed domains fail validation while unsigned ones resolve fine.
recommendation: Update the root trust anchor to the current KSK ('Add-DnsServerTrustAnchor -Root' after enabling automatic RFC 5011 rollover support), then clear the resolver cache; keep automatic trust-anchor updates on.

goal: PXE boot fails -- clients don't receive boot server info though DHCP addressing works
plan: Diagnose the dhcp issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: DHCP options 66 (boot server) and 67 (boot file name) aren't set on the scope, so PXE clients get an IP but no next-server/boot path -- addressing and PXE bootstrap are separate option sets.
recommendation: Set option 66 to the WDS/SCCM PXE server's FQDN and 67 to the boot file (e.g., smsboot\x64\wdsmgfw.efi for UEFI) -- or better, configure IP helpers on routers to forward PXE broadcasts natively, which handles BIOS/UEFI differences more reliably than static options.

goal: DHCP failover partners show different lease data -- clients get NAKs when the partner answers
plan: Diagnose the dhcp issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The failover relationship is out of sync (partner state COMMUNICATION_INTERRUPTED); each server holds divergent lease tables, so a renewal answered by the wrong partner produces a NAK.
recommendation: Restore connectivity between the DHCP partners (port 647 TCP), then resynchronize the relationship ('Invoke-DhcpServerv4FailoverReplication'); investigate what broke the partner channel -- often a firewall change.

goal: Users intermittently get addresses from an unauthorized (rogue) DHCP server on the LAN
plan: Diagnose the dhcp issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Lease obtained from server 192.168.0.1 (not the corporate 10.0.0.10)

summary: A consumer router someone plugged in is answering DHCP DISCOVER faster than the corporate server for nearby clients, handing out its own subnet -- classic rogue DHCP symptom pattern (wrong gateway/subnet on affected machines).
recommendation: Locate and remove the rogue device (trace the offending server's MAC via switch tables), and enable DHCP snooping on managed switches so only authorized ports may answer DHCP -- the durable fix against repeats.

goal: A site binding conflict in HTTP.sys -- 'The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process' on site start
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: URL group with 0.0.0.0:443 registered to PID 3120 (a third-party agent)

summary: HTTP.sys already has the port reserved by another process/URL ACL, so IIS can't add its binding -- with HTTP.sys the conflict is at the kernel URL-reservation layer, not a file at all despite the message.
recommendation: Stop/reconfigure the conflicting process (or remove its stale reservation with 'netsh http delete urlacl'), then start the IIS site; two listeners can't own the same IP:port:host combination in HTTP.sys.

goal: Windows Process Activation Service (WAS) won't start, taking all IIS sites down
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Get-Service WAS, W3SVC | Select-Object Name, Status
steps.stdout:
Name  Status
----  ------
WAS   Stopped
W3SVC Stopped
Configuration error: applicationHost.config line 412: unexpected end tag

summary: WAS fails with a corrupted configuration error -- applicationHost.config has an XML syntax error introduced by a manual edit, and WAS (which parses it before W3SVC can run) refuses to start.
recommendation: Fix the XML at the reported line (or restore applicationHost.config from 'C:\inetpub\history\' which keeps automatic versioned backups), then start WAS and W3SVC.

goal: ASP.NET Core app returns 500.30 'ANCM In-Process Start Failure' in IIS
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Unhandled exception: InvalidOperationException: Connection string 'Main' not found.

summary: The ASP.NET Core Module launched the app in-process and it crashed during startup; stdout logging (disabled by default) captured a missing environment variable that only exists on the dev machine.
recommendation: Enable stdout logging in web.config to capture startup errors, then provide the missing configuration (connection string/env var) via appsettings.Production.json or the app pool's environment settings; disable stdout logging again after diagnosis.

goal: HTTPS works for one site but a second site on the same IP serves the wrong certificate (SNI misconfiguration)
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: IP:port 0.0.0.0:443 (one legacy IP binding) + hostname bindings missing for site2.corp.com

summary: The second site's binding wasn't created with 'Require SNI', so it fell back to the IP-bound default cert -- with multiple TLS sites per IP, every binding except at most one default must use SNI.
recommendation: Recreate site2's HTTPS binding with the hostname filled in and 'Require Server Name Indication' checked, bound to its own certificate; keep only one (or zero) non-SNI fallback binding per IP:port.

goal: Enabling HSTS -- but the site keeps redirecting HTTP to HTTPS inconsistently and browsers don't remember
plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The Strict-Transport-Security header is only being sent on some responses because it's configured on a subfolder's web.config, not site-wide, so browsers never durably record the HSTS policy.
recommendation: Configure HSTS at the site level (IIS 10.0+ has native HSTS settings on the site's HSTS dialog; enable includeSubDomains and an appropriate max-age), and keep exactly one canonical HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect rule.

goal: Clients report 'certificate chain incomplete' for a site whose cert is valid -- missing intermediate CA
plan: Diagnose the certificates issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: A certificate chain could not be built to a trusted root authority (missing intermediate: CorpIssuingCA2)

summary: The server sends only the leaf certificate; clients that lack the intermediate cached fail chain building, while machines that happened to cache it earlier succeed -- classic missing-intermediate deployment error.
recommendation: Install the intermediate CA cert into the server's Intermediate Certification Authorities store (or re-import the full PFX chain) so the server presents the complete chain during the TLS handshake.

goal: A certificate exists but the service can't use it -- 'the credentials supplied to the package were not recognized' (private key missing)
plan: Diagnose the certificates issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where-Object Subject -like '*svc.corp.com*' | Select-Object HasPrivateKey

summary: The certificate's private key is absent (imported from a .cer instead of a .pfx), so any service trying to use it for TLS fails -- the public certificate alone can't terminate connections.
recommendation: Re-import the certificate from its .pfx (which contains the private key) with the correct password, or if the key was generated on this machine, run 'certutil -repairstore my <thumbprint>' to relink the orphaned key.

goal: PFX import fails with 'The password you entered is incorrect' though the password is definitely right
plan: Diagnose the certificates issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Encryption algorithm: AES256-SHA256 (unsupported on this OS build)

summary: The PFX was exported on a newer system using AES-256 encryption, and this legacy server's crypto stack can't decrypt AES-encrypted PFX files -- the misleading 'wrong password' error masks the algorithm mismatch.
recommendation: Re-export the PFX with legacy TripleDES-SHA1 compatibility (the 'Enable certificate privacy' checkbox unticked / '-CryptoAlgorithmOption TripleDES_SHA1' in Export-PfxCertificate), or update/replace the legacy target system.

goal: Certificate auto-enrollment silently stopped -- machine certs expire without renewal
plan: Diagnose the certificates issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Certificate enrollment initiated (completed with no certificates issued)
Enrollment for template 'CorpMachine' failed: access denied

summary: Autoenrollment GPO is enabled but the certificate template's permissions no longer grant this computer group Enroll/Autoenroll after a template modification -- clients poll, find nothing permitted, and log nothing visible.
recommendation: Restore Enroll + Autoenroll permissions for the computers' group on the certificate template (Certification Authority console > template Security tab), then 'certutil -pulse' on clients to trigger immediate re-enrollment.

goal: L2TP/IPsec VPN fails behind home routers with error 809 -- no response from server
plan: Diagnose the vpn issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Error 809 means the IPsec negotiation packets never made it through: the NAT router isn't passing ESP/UDP 4500 properly, and Windows by default won't attempt IPsec over double-NAT without the NAT-T registry setting.
recommendation: Set AssumeUDPEncapsulationContextOnSendRule=2 under PolicyAgent and reboot (enables NAT-T through double NAT), confirm UDP 500/4500 pass the router, and prefer IKEv2/SSTP where possible -- they traverse NAT far better.

goal: SSTP VPN fails with error 0x80092013 'The revocation function was unable to check revocation'
plan: Diagnose the vpn issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: SSTP validates the server certificate's revocation over HTTP before the tunnel exists; on this network the CRL URL is only reachable through the tunnel, creating a chicken-and-egg failure.
recommendation: Publish the CRL on an internet-reachable endpoint (standard practice for SSTP deployments); as a stopgap only, clients can set NoCertRevocationCheck=1 for SSTP -- but fixing CRL reachability is the correct solution.

goal: IKEv2 VPN connects but no traffic flows -- small packets work, large transfers stall (MTU blackhole)
plan: Diagnose the vpn issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The tunnel adds encapsulation overhead and an upstream device drops ICMP 'fragmentation needed', so Path MTU Discovery fails -- TCP handshakes (small) succeed while full-size packets vanish.
recommendation: Lower the VPN interface MTU to the discovered working size ('netsh interface ipv4 set subinterface "VPN" mtu=1350 store=persistent'), and/or enable MSS clamping on the VPN server so all TCP flows self-adjust.

goal: Always On VPN user tunnel never auto-connects for some users after deployment
plan: Diagnose the vpn issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Subject: CN=jdoe ... EKU: Encrypting File System (Client Authentication missing)

summary: The AOVPN profile's trigger relies on the user certificate, and affected users' certs were issued from a template missing the Client Authentication EKU -- the tunnel silently declines to trigger without a valid auth cert.
recommendation: Fix the certificate template to include Client Authentication EKU and re-enroll affected users; AOVPN user tunnels require a client-auth-capable certificate for both triggering and EAP authentication.

goal: WPA2-Enterprise (802.1X) Wi-Fi fails with 'Can't connect to this network' after a NPS server certificate renewal
plan: Diagnose the wifi issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: netsh wlan export profile name='CorpWiFi' folder=C:\temp; Select-String -Path C:\temp\*.xml -Pattern 'TrustedRootCA'
steps.stdout: TrustedRootCA hash matches the OLD issuing CA only

summary: Clients validate the RADIUS server's certificate; the renewed NPS cert came from a different CA than the one configured in the Wi-Fi profile's trusted root list, so clients correctly refuse authentication.
recommendation: Update and redeploy the Wi-Fi profile (GPO/Intune) with the new issuing CA in the trusted roots for server validation, or reissue the NPS certificate from the originally trusted CA; never train users to click through server-validation failures.

goal: Wi-Fi drops every time weather radar is nearby -- 5 GHz DFS channel interruptions
plan: Diagnose the wifi issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The AP uses DFS channels which must vacate immediately when radar signatures are detected; each detection forces a channel switch that clients experience as a drop -- environmental/regulatory behavior, not a fault.
recommendation: Configure the AP to prefer non-DFS channels (36-48, 149-165 where permitted) if drops are frequent at this location; DFS channels offer cleaner spectrum but carry mandatory radar-vacate behavior.

goal: A device can't join Wi-Fi -- MAC filtering blocks it because MAC randomization gives a new address
plan: Diagnose the wifi issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Windows' random hardware address feature presents a per-network randomized MAC, which doesn't match the address whitelisted in the router's MAC filter -- each 'Forget'/'re-add cycle can generate yet another address.
recommendation: Either disable random hardware addresses for this network (Wi-Fi network Properties toggle) and whitelist the true MAC, or preferably drop MAC filtering entirely -- it adds admin burden with negligible security value.

goal: Hyper-V Live Migration fails with 'The credentials supplied to the package were not recognized' between two hosts
plan: Diagnose the hyperv issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Live Migration over Kerberos requires constrained delegation configured on both hosts' computer accounts for the cifs and 'Microsoft Virtual System Migration Service' services -- one host is missing the delegation entries.
recommendation: Add matching constrained delegation entries (use Kerberos-only) on both host computer accounts for each other's migration and cifs services, or switch migration authentication to CredSSP (requires initiating from a console session).

goal: A VM's checkpoint won't merge -- disk space fills up as .avhdx files keep growing
plan: Diagnose the hyperv issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Name: Pre-Update (created 47 days ago, never deleted)
SizeRemaining : 18 GB (chain needs ~60 GB to merge)

summary: The checkpoint's background merge stalled because the volume has too little free space for the merge working set; the .avhdx chain keeps absorbing writes and consuming space, worsening the shortage in a feedback loop.
recommendation: Free or add space on the volume (move another VM's files off temporarily), then delete the checkpoint so the merge can complete; adopt a policy of removing checkpoints within days -- they're not backups.

goal: Dynamic Memory VM gets stuck at its startup RAM and performance craters under load
plan: Diagnose the hyperv issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Get-VMMemory -VMName AppVM | Select-Object DynamicMemoryEnabled, Startup, Maximum
Get-VMIntegrationService -VMName AppVM | Where-Object Name -like '*Memory*' | Select-Object Enabled, PrimaryStatusDescription

summary: Dynamic Memory ballooning requires the guest's Hyper-V memory integration component; this guest's integration services are outdated/disabled, so the host can never expand the VM beyond startup RAM.
recommendation: Enable the memory integration service ('Enable-VMIntegrationService -VMName AppVM -Name "Dynamic Memory"') and update guest integration components via Windows Update in the guest; verify demand-based expansion resumes under load.

goal: A Generation 1 VM can't boot from a copied disk that works in a Generation 2 VM
plan: Diagnose the hyperv issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Get-VHD 'V:\disks\app.vhdx' | Select-Object VhdFormat; Get-Disk -Number 5 | Select-Object PartitionStyle

summary: Gen1 VMs boot via BIOS/MBR while Gen2 requires UEFI/GPT: the disk is GPT-partitioned with an EFI system partition, which Gen1's emulated BIOS can't boot -- the generations aren't interchangeable at the firmware level.
recommendation: Attach the disk to a Generation 2 VM (matching its UEFI/GPT layout), or convert the OS image to MBR/BIOS boot with MBR2GPT-in-reverse tooling/reinstall if Gen1 is truly required (legacy OSes only).

goal: docker compose up fails with 'network ... overlaps with other one on this address space'
plan: Diagnose the docker issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Compose's default bridge subnet collides with the corporate VPN's routes; Docker refuses to create a network whose range overlaps an existing route, and the VPN owns that space on this machine.
recommendation: Set a non-conflicting address pool in Docker's daemon settings ('default-address-pools' e.g. 10.200.0.0/16) and explicit subnets in compose networks; pick ranges the VPN never routes.

goal: Switching between Windows containers and Linux containers breaks builds with 'no matching manifest for windows/amd64'
plan: Diagnose the docker issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The daemon is in Windows-containers mode while the compose/build references Linux-only images; each mode can only run its own OS's images, and the error is the registry saying no Windows variant exists for that image.
recommendation: Switch Docker Desktop back to Linux containers mode for Linux images (or use '--platform linux/amd64' with WSL2 backend which runs both via integration); keep separate compose files if genuinely mixing Windows and Linux workloads.

goal: WSL2 DNS resolution fails inside distros while Windows resolves fine
plan: Diagnose the wsl issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: nameserver 172.28.144.1 (unreachable from inside WSL while VPN active)

summary: WSL2 generates /etc/resolv.conf pointing at the Windows host's virtual DNS proxy, and a VPN client's firewall rules block the WSL NAT subnet from reaching it -- Linux-side DNS dies whenever the VPN is up.
recommendation: Create /etc/wsl.conf with 'generateResolvConf=false', write a static resolv.conf (corporate DNS or 1.1.1.1 per policy), and/or allow the WSL subnet through the VPN client's firewall; 'wsl --shutdown' applies changes.

goal: BitLocker demands recovery key after every BIOS update -- TPM PCR mismatch
plan: Diagnose the bitlocker issue with read-only checks

summary: The default PCR validation profile includes firmware measurements that change with every BIOS update, so the TPM correctly refuses auto-unlock until re-sealed -- expected security behavior, manageable operationally.
recommendation: Before planned firmware updates, suspend BitLocker ('Suspend-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -RebootCount 1') so the update boots without a recovery prompt and protection auto-resumes re-sealed to the new measurements.

summary: Network Unlock requires the WDS-hosted unlock server, DHCP on the boot NIC, the Network Unlock certificate deployed, and UEFI DHCP boot support -- the client here never gets a DHCP lease during pre-boot because the NIC's UEFI network stack is disabled.
recommendation: Enable the UEFI network stack (IPv4 PXE support) in firmware setup so pre-boot DHCP works; verify the Network Unlock server's port 5052/UDP reachability from the client VLAN -- with those in place, PIN is only needed off-network.

goal: BitLocker encryption is stuck 'paused' at a fixed percentage and never resumes
plan: Diagnose the bitlocker issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

summary: Encryption auto-paused due to bad sectors detected on the volume mid-conversion; BitLocker won't resume until the underlying disk errors are addressed, silently waiting rather than surfacing a clear error.
recommendation: Run 'chkdsk D: /r' to map out bad sectors, then 'Resume-BitLocker -MountPoint D:'; if bad blocks keep appearing, the drive is failing -- move data and encrypt a replacement instead.

goal: winget fails with 'Failed in attempting to update the source: winget' -- can't install anything

recommendation: Download the current DesktopAppInstaller .msixbundle from Microsoft's official distribution (or via winget-cli GitHub releases) and install with Add-AppxPackage; then the dependent packages install normally.

goal: Outlook keeps prompting for password after tenant enables Modern Authentication

recommendation: Remove the EnableADAL=0 override (modern auth is default-on in current Office), restart Outlook, and complete the interactive Azure AD sign-in; audit for old GPOs still deploying legacy auth registry values.

goal: A shared mailbox stopped auto-mapping in Outlook for one user while others see it fine

recommendation: Either add the mailbox manually in Outlook (File > Account Settings > More Settings > Advanced), or grant the user direct Full Access with automapping ('Add-MailboxPermission shared -User jdoe -AccessRights FullAccess -AutoMapping $true').

goal: Hybrid Azure AD Join stuck 'pending' -- dsregcmd shows the device isn't registering

goal: Users blocked by Conditional Access with 'You can't get there from here' on compliant-looking devices
plan: Diagnose the azuread issue with read-only checks

recommendation: Fix the MDM enrollment (re-enroll via Settings > Access work or school, or repair the Intune enrollment scheduled tasks), force a sync, and confirm the device flips to Compliant in Intune -- CA unblocks automatically after that.

goal: Windows Autopilot device hangs at 'Securing your hardware' during pre-provisioning
plan: Diagnose the azuread issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause

summary: That phase is TPM attestation: this device's TPM firmware version has a known attestation bug, so the attestation call loops until timeout -- a device-firmware issue, not an Autopilot profile problem.
recommendation: Update the TPM firmware from the OEM's tool to the fixed version, clear the TPM, and re-run pre-provisioning; check the OEM's Autopilot attestation advisory list before large rollouts.

goal: PC loses BIOS settings and shows 'CMOS checksum error - Defaults loaded' at every cold boot
plan: Diagnose the firmware issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: (system date reverted to firmware default epoch after cold start)

summary: The CMOS checksum failing every cold boot means the settings RAM loses power -- the classic dead CR2032 coin cell; settings survive warm reboots (standby power) but die when AC is removed.
recommendation: Replace the CR2032 battery, restore BIOS settings (boot order, XMP, virtualization), and resync the clock; if the error persists with a new battery, the board's RTC circuit needs service.

goal: Wake-on-LAN stopped working after upgrading to a new machine with Modern Standby

recommendation: Enable magic-packet wake on the adapter ('Enable-NetAdapterPowerManagement -Name Ethernet -WakeOnMagicPacket'), and in firmware enable WOL; on Modern Standby laptops also allow network connectivity in standby (on AC at minimum).

recommendation: Keep the mitigations (recommended); if a controlled/air-gapped workload justifies it, specific mitigations can be disabled via documented registry switches -- document the risk acceptance and never do this on internet-facing machines.

goal: One RAM slot no longer works -- installed memory shows half the expected total

recommendation: Verify seating first, test each stick alone in each slot to confirm the dead slot, and update BIOS (memory-training fixes are common); a persistently dead slot is a motherboard repair/replace decision.

goal: NVMe SSD performance collapses during long transfers -- thermal throttling suspected
plan: Diagnose the hardware issue with read-only checks

summary: The NVMe drive hits its thermal limit under sustained writes and throttles hard; performance recovers after cool-down, matching the temperature-driven pattern rather than a firmware or driver fault.

recommendation: Use the e-marked cable shipped with the dock (or a certified 100 W cable), update the dock's firmware, and try another laptop port; persistent flapping with known-good cable and firmware means the dock's PD controller is failing.

recommendation: Restore from backup/replica if possible; standalone last-resort is 'mongod --repair' against a copied data directory (never the only copy). Add a replica set member or scheduled dumps to avoid single-copy risk going forward.

goal: VS Code Remote-SSH connects but immediately drops with 'The process tried to write to a nonexistent pipe'

summary: SDR content inside an HDR signal needs its brightness balance set per display; at the default slider position on this monitor, SDR white maps too low, producing the washed-out look -- calibration, not a defect.
recommendation: Adjust Settings > System > Display > HDR > 'SDR content brightness', run the Windows HDR Calibration app for the display profile, and update to the monitor's latest firmware -- cheap HDR400 panels will always look better with HDR off for desktop work.

goal: Mouse pointer jumps/skips after changing 'Enhance pointer precision'
plan: Diagnose the settings issue with read-only checks

summary: Enhance pointer precision is OS-level acceleration; combined with the gaming mouse's own onboard acceleration profile it double-applies, making movement nonlinear and jumpy.
recommendation: Disable one of the two acceleration layers: turn off Enhance pointer precision (Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Mouse > Additional settings > Pointer Options) or the mouse driver's onboard acceleration -- competitive/gaming setups typically disable the OS one.

goal: Sticky Keys popup keeps interrupting games when Shift is pressed rapidly
plan: Diagnose the settings issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or explain expected behavior
summary: The Sticky Keys activation shortcut (5x Shift) is enabled by default and fires during gameplay; the popup steals focus at exactly the wrong moments.
recommendation: Disable the shortcut under Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard > Sticky keys > 'Keyboard shortcut for Sticky keys'; the accessibility feature stays available from Settings for users who need it.

goal: Auto-brightness keeps changing screen brightness against the user's wishes
plan: Diagnose the settings issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or explain expected behavior
summary: Content Adaptive Brightness Control (CABC) plus the ambient light sensor are both adjusting brightness; the OS slider follows their combined output, appearing to 'fight' the user's setting.
recommendation: Turn off Settings > System > Display > Brightness > 'Change brightness automatically when lighting changes' and 'Help improve battery by optimizing displayed content' (CABC); some laptops need CABC disabled in the vendor's own display utility too.

goal: Wallpaper slideshow stops working when on battery
plan: Diagnose the settings issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or explain expected behavior
summary: Slideshow pauses on battery by design to save power -- the setting 'Pause slideshow when on battery power' ships enabled and is easily overlooked, so it looks broken exactly when unplugged.
recommendation: Turn off the pause-on-battery toggle under Settings > Personalization > Background (or accept the battery saving); no repair needed -- it's an intentional default.

goal: Lock screen shows a black background instead of Spotlight images
plan: Diagnose the settings issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or explain expected behavior
summary: Windows Spotlight's content delivery is blocked because the connected experiences endpoint can't be reached (proxy rule), so Spotlight silently falls back to black instead of erroring.
recommendation: Allow the Spotlight/Content Delivery endpoints through the proxy/firewall, or switch the lock screen to Picture/Slideshow; after unblocking, toggle Spotlight off/on to refresh its cache.

goal: Fonts look blurry/fuzzy after changing display scaling

summary: Apps that don't handle dynamic DPI changes keep rendering at the old scale until restarted, and ClearType tuning is still calibrated for the previous scale -- a re-login plus ClearType pass fixes the softness.
recommendation: Sign out and back in after scaling changes, run cttune.exe (ClearType Text Tuner), and for persistently blurry apps set their High DPI override to 'System (Enhanced)'.

goal: Region format changes (date/decimal separator) don't apply inside some apps
plan: Diagnose the settings issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or explain expected behavior
summary: Win32 apps read region formats at launch, and some cache them per-profile; the new format applies system-wide but running apps and services keep the old culture until restarted -- plus Excel keeps its own separator overrides.
recommendation: Restart affected apps (or sign out/in) after region changes; for Excel specifically check File > Options > Advanced > 'Use system separators'. Server processes need a service restart to pick up new culture.

goal: Location services greyed out for all apps
plan: Diagnose the settings issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause

summary: The master location toggle is disabled at the machine level by policy (HKLM), which cascades: per-app toggles grey out and Find My Device stops -- one switch upstream of everything else.
recommendation: Set the machine-level location consent back to Allow (Settings > Privacy & security > Location > Location services master toggle as admin, or the ConsentStore registry value), then grant per-app access individually.

goal: Background apps disabled globally caused missed mail/calendar notifications

recommendation: Set GlobalUserDisabled back to 0 (or the per-app 'Let this app run in background' to Always/Power optimized under the app's Advanced options); background sync resumes immediately.

goal: Power mode slider missing from Settings on a desktop PC

recommendation: Switch to Balanced ('powercfg /setactive SCHEME_BALANCED') to get the slider back; the slider's Best Performance position matches or exceeds the legacy High Performance scheme on modern builds.

goal: Get Help / Feedback Hub and other inbox apps open then immediately close
plan: Diagnose the settings issue with read-only checks

goal: Sound output per-app routing lost after every restart

Apply the appropriate fix or explain expected behavior
summary: Per-app output device assignments in the Volume mixer are stored per audio endpoint ID; the USB DAC re-enumerates with a new ID at each boot (hub timing), so mappings orphan and reset.
recommendation: Plug the DAC directly into a rear motherboard port (stable enumeration), or set it as the system default device instead of per-app mappings; per-app routing sticks only while the endpoint ID stays constant.

goal: Camera works in the Camera app but shows black in browser video calls

recommendation: Uninstall/disable the vendor camera enhancement suite (keep the plain UVC driver), then restart the browser; also confirm the browser's own site permission and Windows camera privacy toggles.

goal: Copilot/search hardware key on a new laptop does nothing

recommendation: Install the OEM's hotkey/system utility package from the vendor support page (or remap the key with PowerToys Keyboard Manager to any function you prefer).

goal: Dynamic refresh rate (DRR) option missing on a 120Hz laptop panel

recommendation: Update the GPU driver to a current WDDM 3.0+ release from the vendor; 'Dynamic (60Hz or 120Hz)' appears in Advanced display settings once the driver capability is present.

recommendation: On an organization device, request the change from IT (the policy owner). On a personal machine, remove the stray OneDrive policy keys, then Settings > OneDrive > Manage Backup > stop backup per folder -- files return to the local profile paths.

recommendation: Clear both layers: 'netsh winhttp reset proxy' plus setting ProxyEnable=0 under HKCU Internet Settings, then restart the browsers; a leftover PAC/AutoConfigURL value should also be removed if present.

goal: Chrome/Edge downloads always fail at the last second with 'Failed - Network error' on large files

steps.stdout: Disk 2 is now the selected disk.
DiskPart succeeded in cleaning the disk.
(runs for several hours on large disks; writes zeros to every sector)

summary: 'clean' only removes partition/volume metadata, leaving all data recoverable; 'clean all' zeroes every sector, which is why it took hours on a 2 TB disk while clean returned instantly.
recommendation: Use 'clean' for reuse within your own environment, 'clean all' before disposal or transfer of ownership; note 'clean all' on SSDs is unnecessary wear -- a secure-erase/ATA sanitize via the vendor tool is better.

summary: OEM/EFI/recovery partitions carry a protection flag, so plain delete is refused; the override parameter is required and exists specifically to make the destructive intent explicit.
recommendation: Before using override, confirm WinRE isn't hosted there ('reagentc /info') -- deleting an in-use recovery partition silently breaks Reset/Advanced Startup until WinRE is re-registered elsewhere.

recommendation: Clear the attribute at the disk level, and if a single volume is still read-only clear it separately with 'attributes volume clear readonly'; check for a physical write-protect switch on SD cards and USB sticks first.

recommendation: If the letter is already taken, 'assign letter=' with a free letter or remove it from the other volume first; letters persist per-volume in the mount manager database, so this survives reboots.

recommendation: Record the volume GUID from 'mountvol' before removing the letter so scripts and services can still address it; removing a letter does not unmount or affect data in any way.

recommendation: Mark the small System Reserved partition active, not the Windows partition; 'active' applies to MBR only -- on GPT/UEFI systems the equivalent is having a correctly typed EFI System Partition.

recommendation: The EFI partition must be FAT32 and at least ~100 MB (260 MB is the modern recommendation for 4Kn compatibility); after bcdboot, remove the temporary letter with 'remove letter=S'.

goal: Converting a disk to GPT with diskpart -- 'The specified disk is not convertible' error

summary: diskpart's convert command requires an empty disk; existing partitions block it, which is why the error appears even though the disk is otherwise healthy.
recommendation: Either back up and 'clean' the disk first then convert, or use MBR2GPT for an in-place conversion that preserves data on the OS disk; diskpart's convert is destructive by requirement.

goal: Automount is disabled so new volumes never get drive letters automatically

summary: Automount was turned off (common on servers and after imaging work), so every newly attached volume mounts without a letter until assigned manually.
recommendation: Re-enable automount, then run 'automount scrub' to clear stale mount-point entries for volumes that no longer exist -- those stale entries are what block letters from being reused.

goal: 'list disk' shows no disks at all inside WinRE

recommendation: Load the vendor's storage driver in WinRE with drvload then rescan, or switch the BIOS from RAID/VMD to AHCI if the OS was installed that way; installation media with the driver slipstreamed avoids this entirely.

summary: Extend requires unallocated space immediately after the selected partition; the free space sits before it, so diskpart correctly reports it as unusable for this operation.
recommendation: Move or remove the partition sitting between the volume and the free space (a third-party tool can relocate it), or extend a different volume that is adjacent; diskpart cannot move partitions.

summary: Querying the maximum first showed only a fraction of the free space is reclaimable, explaining why shrink appeared to 'ignore' the free space -- immovable files cap the reclaimable region.
recommendation: Always run 'shrink querymax' first; to raise the ceiling, disable hibernation, move the page file, and delete shadow copies, then re-query before shrinking.

goal: Changing a partition type ID so Windows stops treating a data partition as recovery
