recommendation: Clear 'Read-only recommended' in File > Save As > Tools > General Options; with no owner file present and the file not marked read-only on disk, the flag inside the workbook is the only remaining cause.

recommendation: Restart WSL so the virtual network is rebuilt; if it recurs on every VPN connect, set the VPN client to allow local network access or use mirrored networking mode in .wslconfig.

goal: A laptop fan runs at full speed immediately after boot and never slows down

recommendation: Perform an EC reset: shut down, disconnect power and hold the power button for 30 seconds (or use the vendor's pinhole reset), then boot; with the CPU idle at 3% the fan behaviour is controller state rather than load.

recommendation: The inspection CA certificate has expired - renew it through the security product, or disable HTTPS scanning; a reachable port 443 with universal TLS failures always points at the inspecting middlebox.

recommendation: Set the lid action to Sleep on both AC and battery, and fix the backup agent's power request - update it or configure it not to hold the system awake. This combination is a genuine overheating risk, not just wasted battery.

goal: I press a key to wake it up and nothing happens - I have to hold the power button
plan: Check what is permitted to wake the machine
Confirm the last wake source
Identify why input does not wake it

steps.stdout:
Wake History Count - 1
Wake History [0]
  Wake Source Count - 1
  Wake Source [0]
    Type: Power Button

Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     HID Keyboard Device

summary: No device is armed to wake the machine at all - the wake_armed list is empty. The keyboard is healthy, but its wake capability has been disabled, so the power button is the only remaining wake source. That matches the wake history showing only power-button wakes.
recommendation: Enable 'Allow this device to wake the computer' on the keyboard and mouse in Device Manager's Power Management tab. This often gets disabled by power-saving tools or after a driver update.

feedback.note: keyboard wake was unticked, works with a keypress now

goal: Hibernate has disappeared from the shutdown menu
plan: Check whether hibernation is enabled at system level
Confirm the hibernation file exists
Re-enable if appropriate

steps.stdout:
The following sleep states are available on this system:
    Standby (S3)

The following sleep states are not available on this system:
    Hibernate
        Hibernation has not been enabled.

summary: Hibernation is switched off at system level and the hibernation file has been removed - which is why the option vanished from the menu rather than being greyed out. This is usually done deliberately to reclaim disk space, since hiberfil.sys is sized against installed RAM.
recommendation: Run 'powercfg /h on' from an elevated prompt to restore it, then tick Hibernate under Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do. It will consume roughly 40% of your RAM size in disk space; with 64 GB free that is not a concern here.

feedback.note: someone had turned it off to save space, back now

goal: My PC wakes up in the middle of the night by itself
plan: Find what woke it
Check for scheduled wake timers
Decide whether to permit or block it

steps.stdout:
Wake History Count - 1
Wake History [0]
  Wake Source Count - 1
  Wake Source [0]
    Type: Wake Timer
    Owner: [SERVICE] \Device\HarddiskVolume3\Windows\System32\svchost.exe (SystemEventsBroker)
    Owner Supplied Reason: Windows will execute 'NT TASK\Microsoft\Windows\UpdateOrchestrator\Reboot'
Timer set by [SERVICE] ... UpdateOrchestrator\Reboot expires at 3:00:00 AM

summary: Windows Update sets a wake timer so it can install updates and restart at 03:00. This is deliberate behaviour, not a fault - the machine wakes, does its work, and goes back to sleep or restarts depending on what is pending.
recommendation: If you would rather it did not, disable 'Allow wake timers' in the active power plan's sleep settings and widen your active hours so updates install while you are using the machine. Blocking wake timers means updates wait for you to be at the keyboard.

feedback.note: turned off wake timers, updates can wait until I'm using it

goal: Fan spins up loudly for a few minutes every time I sit down at the PC in the morning
plan: Identify what runs shortly after logon
Check whether it is scheduled or triggered
Decide whether it is expected

steps.command: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskPath '\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Defender\' | Get-ScheduledTaskInfo | Select-Object TaskName, LastRunTime, LastTaskResult
steps.stdout:
TaskName                        LastRunTime          LastTaskResult
--------                        -----------          --------------
Windows Defender Scheduled Scan 8/14/2026 8:44:02 AM              0

steps.command: Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 3 Name, CPU

summary: Defender's scheduled scan is configured to run at idle, and the first idle window it finds each day is shortly after you sign in. The scan is doing exactly what it should - the fan noise is the CPU working, not a fault.
recommendation: Move the scheduled scan to a fixed time when you are not at the machine, such as lunchtime or overnight if it stays on. Do not disable it; a daily quick scan costs a few minutes of fan noise and is worth keeping.

feedback.note: moved it to 1pm, mornings are quiet now

goal: Windows Update says it failed but doesn't tell me anything useful
plan: Get the actual error code from the update history
Check the servicing components it depends on
Address the specific failure

steps.stdout: Installation Failure: Windows failed to install the following update with error 0x80070005: 2026-08 Cumulative Update.

steps.command: Get-Service wuauserv, bits, cryptsvc, msiserver | Select-Object Name, Status
steps.stdout:
Name      Status
----      ------
wuauserv Running
bits     Running
cryptsvc Running
msiserver Stopped

summary: The real error is 0x80070005, which is access denied - the update could not write where it needed to. The Windows Installer service is stopped, and the update requires it to service installer-based components.
recommendation: Start msiserver and set it to Manual, then retry the update. If 0x80070005 returns with all services running, third-party antivirus is usually blocking access to the servicing folders - pause it for the install.

feedback.note: installer service was disabled, update went through after

goal: Windows says my drive has a problem and wants to scan it - should I let it?
plan: Establish what triggered the prompt
Check the volume and the physical disk separately
Decide whether scanning is safe

steps.command: Get-PhysicalDisk | Where-Object DeviceId -eq 1 | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter | Select-Object ReadErrorsTotal, Wear, PowerOnHours

summary: The dirty bit is set, which is what triggers the prompt - it happens after an unclean shutdown while files were open. The underlying hardware is fine: zero read errors, 2% wear, no disk events. This is a file-system consistency check, not a failing drive.
recommendation: Yes, let it scan - with healthy hardware chkdsk is low risk and clears the flag. The answer would be different on a drive reporting read errors, where scanning can stress failing media; that is why the physical disk was checked before agreeing.

feedback.note: ran the scan, took 10 minutes, warning gone

goal: The internet works on my phone but not on the desktop, both on the same network
plan: Compare the two paths rather than assuming the network is down
Check the desktop's own configuration
Find where it differs

steps.stdout:
Name     Status LinkSpeed
----     ------ ---------
Ethernet Up     100 Mbps

Name    Enabled DefaultOutboundAction
----    ------- ---------------------
Private    True                 Block

summary: Addressing is correct and the router responds, so the local network is fine - which matches the phone working. The desktop's firewall has its default outbound action set to Block on the Private profile, so nothing can leave the machine beyond the local subnet.
recommendation: Set the outbound default back to Allow for the Private profile. Blocking outbound by default is a deliberate hardening choice that requires an allow rule for every application - it is almost certainly not what was intended here.

feedback.note: a 'security' tool had set that, reverted it

goal: The mouse pointer jumps to the corner of the screen on its own
plan: Check which pointing devices are active
Look for a second device generating input
Isolate the source

steps.stdout:
Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     HID-compliant mouse
OK     Synaptics Precision TouchPad
OK     USB Input Device

steps.command: Get-PnpDevice -Class HIDClass | Where-Object FriendlyName -like '*game*' | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
steps.stdout:
Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     USB Gaming Controller

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_PointingDevice | Select-Object Name, Status | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count

summary: Three pointing devices are active, and one of them is a game controller whose analogue stick is drifting. Windows treats a controller with mouse emulation as a pointing device, so a stick resting slightly off-centre pushes the cursor continuously toward one corner.
recommendation: Unplug the controller to confirm, then either recalibrate its dead zone in the vendor software or disable its mouse emulation. The mouse itself is not faulty - this is a second device competing for the same cursor.

feedback.note: it was the Xbox controller left plugged in behind the monitor

goal: Some keys on my keyboard type numbers instead of letters
plan: Check whether an alternate layer is active
Confirm the keyboard layout
Distinguish hardware from a mode

steps.stdout:
Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     HID Keyboard Device

summary: The layout is correct and the keyboard is healthy. The affected keys are the ones that double as an embedded numeric keypad on this compact keyboard - Num Lock is on, which switches U I O J K L M into numbers. It is a keyboard mode, not a fault or a layout problem.
recommendation: Press Num Lock (often Fn + Num Lock on compact keyboards) to turn it off. Laptops without a separate numeric pad use this embedded layer, which is why it looks like specific keys have broken rather than a whole section.

feedback.note: never knew that layer existed, one keypress fixed it

goal: The touchpad stops working every time I plug in a mouse
plan: Check whether the touchpad device is still present
Look for a disable-on-external-pointer setting
Confirm the behaviour is configured

steps.stdout:
Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     Synaptics Precision TouchPad
OK     HID-compliant mouse

summary: The touchpad device is healthy and still enumerated. Windows is deliberately disabling it when an external mouse is connected, because the 'Leave touchpad on when a mouse is connected' option is off - a setting, not a fault.
recommendation: Tick that option under Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Touchpad. Some vendor utilities have their own equivalent setting that overrides the Windows one, so check there too if it reverts.

feedback.note: one tickbox, wish I'd found it months ago

goal: My pen writes but the pressure sensitivity doesn't work in any app
plan: Confirm the pen is recognised as a pressure-capable device
Check which driver stack is handling it
Identify what is missing

steps.command: Get-PnpDevice -Class HIDClass | Where-Object FriendlyName -match 'Pen|Wacom|Digitizer' | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
Get-CimInstance Win32_PnPSignedDriver | Where-Object DeviceName -match 'pen|digitizer' | Select-Object DeviceName, DriverProviderName
Get-Service | Where-Object DisplayName -match 'Wacom|Tablet' | Select-Object Name, Status

summary: The pen works through the generic Microsoft HID driver, which reports position and contact but not the vendor's pressure curve. No tablet service is installed, so applications receive a binary touch rather than graded pressure values.
recommendation: Install the pen manufacturer's driver and its tablet service - pressure is delivered through that stack, not the in-box HID driver. Applications also need to be set to use Windows Ink or the vendor API, whichever the driver exposes.

feedback.note: Wacom driver installed, pressure works everywhere now

goal: The USB hub works but devices plugged into it keep disconnecting
plan: Check the hub and its downstream devices
Look at the power configuration
Determine whether it is power or data

steps.command: Get-PnpDevice -Class USB | Where-Object FriendlyName -match 'Hub' | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
steps.stdout:
Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     Generic USB Hub
OK     USB Root Hub (USB 3.0)

summary: The hub itself stays connected while downstream devices repeatedly disappear and re-enumerate. That pattern - the hub fine, its children dropping - is a power delivery problem: a bus-powered hub sharing 500 mA across several devices that each want more.
recommendation: Use a hub with its own power supply, particularly for external drives and anything that charges. Also disable USB selective suspend for that root hub, since power-saving on a marginal power budget makes the drops more frequent.

feedback.note: powered hub sorted it completely

goal: Some video files play with sound but no picture
plan: Check which codec the files need
Confirm what is installed
Identify the missing component
summary: Audio plays because the audio codec is present, but the video track uses HEVC (H.265) and the HEVC extension is not installed. VP9 and WebM extensions are there, which is why other files play normally - it is specific to this codec.
recommendation: Install the HEVC Video Extensions from the Microsoft Store. Phone footage from recent iPhones and many Android devices defaults to HEVC, which is why this appears suddenly after changing phone rather than gradually.

feedback.note: new phone records in HEVC, extension fixed it

goal: Thumbnails don't show for my photos and videos, just generic icons
plan: Check whether thumbnails are disabled by setting
Look at the thumbnail cache state
Distinguish a setting from corruption
summary: The thumbnail cache is present and healthy at 284 MB, so nothing is corrupted. IconsOnly is set to 1, which explicitly tells Explorer to show file-type icons instead of previews - this is the 'Always show icons, never thumbnails' folder option.
recommendation: Uncheck 'Always show icons, never thumbnails' under Folder Options > View. Clearing the thumbnail cache would have achieved nothing here, which is why the setting was checked before assuming corruption.

feedback.note: a cleanup tool had ticked that to 'save space'

goal: Fonts render with jagged edges and look wrong at small sizes
plan: Check whether font smoothing is enabled
Look at the ClearType configuration
Confirm the display scaling
summary: Font smoothing is switched off entirely - both the master setting and the ClearType type are zero. On a 1440p display at 100% scaling this produces exactly the hard, jagged edges described. Nothing is broken; anti-aliasing has been disabled.
recommendation: Re-enable it through Adjust ClearType text in the Start menu search, which sets both values and lets you tune it for your panel. Performance-tuning guides often disable font smoothing for a negligible gain and a very visible cost.

feedback.note: a 'gaming optimiser' had turned it off

goal: Windows is in English but some apps show a different language
plan: Check the display language and the regional format separately
Look at the app-specific language list
Identify which setting each app follows

steps.stdout:
LanguageTag Autonym
----------- -------
en-GB       English (United Kingdom)
de-DE       Deutsch

summary: The Windows UI is English, but the system locale - which non-Unicode and some older applications follow - is still German from the original installation. Applications that read the system locale rather than the UI language display German.
recommendation: Change the system locale to English under Region settings > Administrative > Change system locale, then reboot. This is separate from both the display language and the regional format, which is why changing the visible language did not affect these apps.

feedback.note: laptop was bought in Germany, that explains it

goal: Dates show as month/day and I want day/month, but changing the language didn't help
plan: Check the regional format separately from the display language
Confirm which controls date presentation
Correct the right setting

steps.stdout:
Name  DisplayName        ShortDate
----  -----------        ---------
en-US English (United States) M/d/yyyy

summary: The display language is English (UK) and the country is set to United Kingdom, but the regional format - which is what actually controls date, time, number and currency presentation - is still English (United States). Those are three independent settings.
recommendation: Change 'Regional format' to English (United Kingdom) under Settings > Time & language > Language & region. The display language governs menu text; the regional format governs how data is written.

feedback.note: three different settings, no wonder I couldn't find it

goal: My keyboard keeps switching layouts while I'm typing
plan: List the installed input methods
Check the switching hotkey
Remove what is not needed

steps.command: Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Keyboard Layout\Toggle' -Name Hotkey, Language Hotkey -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

summary: Three input methods are installed - UK, US and French - and the layout-switching hotkey is enabled. Left Alt + Shift is easy to press accidentally while reaching for other shortcuts, which cycles through all three mid-sentence.
recommendation: Remove the layouts you do not use, and set the switching hotkey to Not Assigned under Advanced keyboard settings. Keeping one spare layout is fine if you need it; three plus an accidental hotkey is what causes this.

feedback.note: removed French and US, no more surprises

goal: Games run at a much lower frame rate than they used to on the same settings
plan: Check which GPU the game is actually using
Look at the power profile in effect
Identify what changed

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name, CurrentRefreshRate, AdapterRAM
steps.stdout:
Name                       CurrentRefreshRate    AdapterRAM
----                       ------------------    ----------
Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630                  60    1073741824
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060                    60   12884901888

summary: Two problems compound each other. The active power plan is Power saver, which caps the CPU at 1.2 GHz of a possible 4.7, and the display is running at 60 Hz. Neither is a graphics fault - the GPU is present and healthy, it is being starved by the CPU.
recommendation: Switch to Balanced or High performance, and set the display to its full refresh rate in Advanced display settings. Also confirm the game is assigned to the NVIDIA GPU under Graphics settings rather than 'Let Windows decide'.

feedback.note: power plan had reset after an update

goal: Game audio and video are out of sync when I stream or record
plan: Check the capture path and hardware acceleration
Look at sample rate mismatches between devices
Identify the drift source

steps.stdout:
Name             Status
----             ------
NVIDIA Virtual Audio OK
Realtek(R) Audio     OK

steps.command: Get-PnpDevice -Class AudioEndpoint | Where-Object Status -eq 'OK' | Select-Object FriendlyName

summary: Two audio devices are in the capture path running at different sample rates - the Realtek output at 48 kHz and the USB microphone at 44.1 kHz. The recorder resamples one of them, and the small timing error accumulates over a long session, which is why the drift grows rather than being constant.
recommendation: Set both devices to the same sample rate in each one's Advanced properties, 48 kHz being the usual choice. A constant offset would point at encoder latency instead, which is corrected with a fixed audio delay in the recording software.

feedback.note: both at 48 kHz and the drift stopped

goal: Game crashes to desktop after a few minutes with no error message
plan: Check whether Windows recorded a crash
Look at temperatures and clocks under load
Distinguish a game fault from a system one

steps.stdout:
Faulting application name: game.exe
Faulting module name: nvwgf2umx.dll
Exception code: 0xc0000005

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name, DriverVersion, DriverDate
steps.stdout:
Name                    DriverVersion DriverDate
----                    ------------- ----------
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 31.0.15.3623  2023-05-11

summary: The crash is recorded and names the NVIDIA Direct3D runtime module rather than the game's own code, with an access violation. There are no display driver timeouts, so the GPU is not resetting - the driver is faulting inside the rendering path.
recommendation: Clean-install the current NVIDIA driver with DDU, and reset any GPU overclock to stock before testing. A crash inside nvwgf2umx.dll with no TDR events is a driver bug or instability rather than a game file problem, so verifying game files will not help.

feedback.note: driver was two years old, clean install fixed it

goal: VirtualBox says VT-x is not available even though my CPU supports it
plan: Confirm the CPU capability
Check whether another hypervisor holds it
Identify what is claiming virtualization

steps.stdout:
Name                    VirtualizationFirmwareEnabled
----                    -----------------------------
12th Gen Intel Core i7                           True

summary: Virtualization is enabled in firmware, but Hyper-V is running and holds the hardware virtualization extensions exclusively - and Virtualization-based Security is also active, which keeps the hypervisor loaded even if the Hyper-V role is removed.
recommendation: Modern VirtualBox versions can run on top of Hyper-V, though slower - updating VirtualBox is the least disruptive option. Disabling the hypervisor entirely would also disable VBS, Credential Guard, WSL2 and Docker Desktop, so weigh that before doing it.

feedback.note: updated VirtualBox rather than turning off Hyper-V

goal: A virtual machine runs extremely slowly compared to the host
plan: Check the VM's allocated resources
Look at whether integration components are current
Check for host-side contention

steps.command: Get-VM -Name 'DevVM' | Select-Object Name, State, CPUUsage, MemoryAssigned, ProcessorCount
steps.stdout:
Name  State   CPUUsage MemoryAssigned ProcessorCount
----  -----   -------- -------------- --------------
DevVM Running       98     2147483648              1

summary: The VM has a single virtual processor on a 16-thread host and is pinned at 98% CPU, with only 2 GB of memory assigned. It is not being starved by the host - it simply has not been given enough resources to do the work being asked of it.
recommendation: Increase the processor count to 4 and memory to 8 GB while the VM is shut down. Do not assign all 16 threads; leaving headroom for the host prevents the whole machine becoming unresponsive under VM load.

feedback.note: 4 vCPU and 8 GB made it usable

goal: Group Policy settings apply on desktops but not on laptops
plan: Compare policy application between the two
Check when laptops last processed policy
Identify what differs about them

steps.command: gpresult /r /scope:computer | Select-String 'Last time Group Policy was applied'
steps.stdout: Last time Group Policy was applied: 8/2/2026 at 9:14:02 AM

Flags: 0
Trusted DC Name \\dc01.corp.local
The command completed successfully

summary: The laptops last applied policy two weeks ago. NETLOGON reports failures at each boot because they start on home Wi-Fi with no line of sight to a domain controller, and by the time the VPN connects the policy refresh window has passed.
recommendation: Enable 'Always wait for the network at computer startup and logon' for laptops, or deploy an always-on VPN that connects before logon. Without one of those, remote machines only get policy when they happen to be on the corporate network at refresh time.

feedback.note: always-on VPN sorted the whole fleet

goal: Mapped drives show a red X but the files open if I click into them
plan: Check the mapping state
Test whether the server is genuinely reachable
Explain the discrepancy
summary: The server is reachable and the share works - the red X is Explorer showing a cached status, not a live one. The session was idle-disconnected by the server after 15 minutes, and Explorer does not re-check until something touches the path, which is exactly what clicking into it does.
recommendation: This is cosmetic and the reconnection is automatic. If it bothers users, raise the server's AutoDisconnectTimeout, or disable the Explorer status caching - but the drive is not actually broken at any point.

feedback.note: explained it to the team, saved a lot of tickets

goal: Updates install fine on most machines but one keeps failing with different errors each time
plan: Check whether the failures share a cause despite different codes
Look at the servicing stack health
Check the underlying storage

steps.stdout:
Installation Failure ... error 0x80070570
Installation Failure ... error 0x8007000D
Installation Failure ... error 0x80073712
The device has a bad block (3 events)

summary: The error codes differ but all three mean corrupted or unreadable data - 0x80070570, 0x8007000D and 0x80073712 are variations on the same theme. The disk is reporting 284 read errors and logging bad blocks, so the component store keeps getting damaged faster than DISM can repair it.
recommendation: Repairing the component store will not hold on failing media. Back up this machine now and replace the drive; varied update errors on one machine while others succeed is a storage symptom, not an update problem.

feedback.note: drive replaced, updates installed first time after that

goal: An internal website shows a certificate warning on new laptops but not older ones
plan: Compare the trust chain between machines
Check whether the issuing CA is trusted
Identify what the older machines have

steps.stdout: A certificate chain could not be built to a trusted root authority

steps.command: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\Root | Where-Object Subject -like '*Corp Root CA*' | Select-Object Subject, NotAfter
steps.stderr: (root CA not present in this machine's store)

summary: The internal root CA certificate is missing from the new laptops' trusted root store. Older machines have it because they were on the domain when the certificate was distributed by policy; the new ones have never received it, and no certificate policy is currently applying to them.
recommendation: Distribute the root CA through Group Policy or Intune so every machine gets it automatically. Installing it manually on each laptop works but will not cover the next batch - and it must go into the machine store, not the user store, for site trust.

feedback.note: added it to the GPO, new builds get it now

goal: Event ID 1014 appears constantly but the internet seems fine
plan: Check what name is timing out
Compare against the configured resolvers
Decide whether it matters

steps.stdout: Name resolution for the name wpad.corp.local timed out after none of the configured DNS servers responded.

summary: Every timeout is for wpad - the automatic proxy discovery name. No proxy is configured and none is needed, so the lookups fail harmlessly and browsing is unaffected. This is log noise, not a fault.
recommendation: Turn off 'Automatically detect settings' in Internet Options to stop the lookups entirely. It is worth doing not for performance but because WPAD is an attack vector on untrusted networks - a malicious responder can become your proxy.

feedback.note: turned off auto-detect, log is quiet and it's safer

goal: Event ID 10 from WMI fills the log after every restart
plan: Identify the failing WMI subscription
Determine what registered it
Decide whether it can be removed

steps.stdout: Event filter with query "SELECT * FROM __InstanceModificationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA 'Win32_Processor'" could not be reactivated

Name       Query
----       -----
SCM Event Log Filter  SELECT * FROM __InstanceModificationEvent...

summary: This is a known benign WMI subscription that fails to reactivate at boot on some builds - it queries processor state and errors because of a namespace permission quirk. It has one legitimate binding and does not indicate a fault or a compromise.
recommendation: This specific filter is documented as harmless and can be ignored. Do note that malicious WMI subscriptions look structurally similar, so it is worth confirming the query and consumer are the known Microsoft ones rather than dismissing every Event 10 by default.

feedback.note: checked the binding matched the documented one

goal: Event ID 1530 keeps appearing at logoff and shutdowns are slow
plan: Identify which process holds the user hive
Correlate with the shutdown delay
Address the holder

steps.command: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Application'; ProviderName='Microsoft-Windows-User Profiles Service'; Id=1530} -MaxEvents 3 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Message
steps.stdout:
Windows detected your registry file is still in use by other applications or services.
 3 user registry handles leaked from ...\Registry\User\S-1-5-21-...:
 Process 6120 (\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Program Files\SyncTool\sync.exe)

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_StartupCommand | Where-Object Command -match 'SyncTool' | Select-Object Name, Location

summary: The event names the specific process holding the hive open: a sync tool started from the user's Run key. Windows waits for it to release the registry at logoff, times out, and unloads forcibly - that wait is the slow shutdown.
recommendation: Update the sync tool, or run it as a machine service rather than a per-user startup item so it does not hold the user hive at all. Occasional 1530 events are harmless; every logoff plus a delay means a real handle leak worth fixing.

feedback.note: vendor had an update that fixed the handle leak

goal: Application install fails with error 0x80070643 but the .NET repair tool says everything is fine
plan: Get the underlying MSI error rather than the wrapper code
Check the installer log
Address the real failure

steps.stdout: Product: AppSuite -- Error 1935. An error occurred during the installation of assembly component. HRESULT: 0x80070005

summary: 0x80070643 is the generic installer failure; the MSI log carries the real one - error 1935 with access denied while installing an assembly. TrustedInstaller is disabled, and assembly installation requires it, so the component cannot be registered.
recommendation: Set TrustedInstaller back to Manual and retry. Always read the MsiInstaller event rather than the code the installer displays - 0x80070643 covers dozens of distinct causes and is not actionable by itself.

feedback.note: someone had disabled TrustedInstaller as a 'tweak'

goal: Network share access fails with error 0x80004005 on one machine only
plan: Check the SMB protocol versions in use
Compare against the server's requirements
Identify the negotiation failure

steps.stdout:
EnableSMB1Protocol       : False
EnableSMB2Protocol       : True
RequireSecuritySignature : True

summary: The port is open, so this is not connectivity. This client requires SMB signing while the NAS does not support it, so negotiation fails and surfaces as the generic 0x80004005. Other machines connect because they have not had signing enforced.
recommendation: The correct fix is a NAS firmware update that supports SMB signing. Turning off RequireSecuritySignature on the client would work but removes protection against relay attacks - do that only as a temporary measure with a date to revisit it.

feedback.note: NAS firmware update added signing support

goal: Windows Backup fails with error 0x807800C5 every time
plan: Check what the backup target reports
Look at the VSS provider state
Identify the specific blocker

steps.stdout: The backup operation ... failed with following error code '0x807800C5' (There was a failure in preparing the backup image of one of the volumes)

State: [1] Stable
State: [5] Waiting for completion
State: [1] Stable

steps.command: Get-Volume | Where-Object DriveType -eq 'Fixed' | Select-Object DriveLetter, FileSystem, HealthStatus
steps.stdout:
DriveLetter FileSystem HealthStatus
----------- ---------- ------------
C           NTFS       Healthy
D           ReFS       Healthy

summary: One VSS writer is stuck waiting for completion rather than stable, and the D volume is formatted ReFS. Windows Backup cannot create a shadow copy of a ReFS volume, which is exactly what 0x807800C5 reports - a failure preparing the backup image of a volume.
recommendation: Exclude the ReFS volume from the backup set, or back it up with a tool that supports ReFS. Also restart the stuck VSS writer's owning service; a writer left waiting will cause intermittent failures even on supported volumes.

feedback.note: excluded the ReFS drive and it completed

goal: Remote PowerShell fails with 0x80090322 'The token supplied to the function is invalid'
plan: Check the authentication method in use
Look at the SPN registration
Identify the Kerberos failure

steps.stdout:
Registered ServicePrincipalNames for CN=SRV04,...:
        HOST/SRV04
        HOST/srv04.corp.local

summary: WinRM responds and Kerberos is enabled, but no WSMAN service principal name is registered for the target - so the ticket request cannot be satisfied for that service and the token is rejected. HOST SPNs alone do not cover WSMAN in every configuration.
recommendation: Register the WSMAN SPN with 'setspn -S WSMAN/srv04.corp.local SRV04'. If the machine is reached by an alias, register the SPN for that name too - Kerberos matches on the exact name the client requested.

feedback.note: registering the SPN fixed it immediately

goal: Every attempt to install a driver fails with 0x800F024B
plan: Check the driver store's health
Look at whether the package is signed appropriately
Identify what rejects it
summary: The catalogue file's signature does not match the package contents - a hash mismatch. That happens when files are edited after signing, or when the download was incomplete. Windows rejects the package rather than installing an unverifiable driver.
recommendation: Re-download the driver package from the vendor and check its size against what they publish. Never work around this with test signing or signature enforcement disabled on a production machine - a driver whose hash does not match is not one to trust.

feedback.note: the download was truncated, second attempt worked

goal: Copying large files fails partway with an I/O error but small files are fine
plan: Check whether the failures cluster on one device
Look at the reliability counters
Determine whether it is media or transport

steps.stdout: The device, \Device\Harddisk2\DR2, has a bad block. (5 events, same device)

steps.command: Get-PhysicalDisk | Select-Object DeviceId, FriendlyName, HealthStatus, BusType
steps.stdout:
DeviceId FriendlyName    HealthStatus BusType
-------- ------------    ------------ -------
2        Seagate Exp 4TB  Warning      USB

summary: All five bad-block events name the same USB drive, which reports Warning health and 47 uncorrected read errors over 38,000 hours. Small files succeed because they happen to land on good sectors; large files span enough of the disk to hit a bad one.
recommendation: Stop writing to this drive. Copy what you still need off it now, largest and most important first, and expect some files to fail. Uncorrected read errors mean data is already unrecoverable in those sectors - the drive should be replaced, not repaired.

feedback.note: got most of it off, a few videos were unrecoverable

goal: I can see a folder but get access denied when I try to open it
plan: Check the effective permissions rather than the owner
Look for an explicit deny
Identify what blocks access

steps.stdout:
IdentityReference    FileSystemRights AccessControlType
-----------------    ---------------- -----------------
BUILTIN\Users        ReadAndExecute              Allow
CORP\Contractors     FullControl                  Deny

summary: There is an Allow for Users and an explicit Deny for Contractors, and the account is in both groups. Deny always takes precedence over Allow in NTFS regardless of order, so membership of Contractors overrides the Users permission entirely.
recommendation: The folder owner needs to either remove the account from Contractors or narrow the Deny entry. Nothing can be changed locally - and adding more Allow permissions would have no effect while the Deny exists.

feedback.note: was in a contractor group from an old project

goal: Windows says the file name is too long even though it looks short
plan: Measure the full path rather than the file name
Check whether long paths are enabled
Identify where the length comes from
summary: The file name is short but the full path is 271 characters, past the 260-character limit that applies while long path support is disabled. Deeply nested project folders accumulate this quietly until one more subfolder tips a file over the edge.
recommendation: Enable LongPathsEnabled and reboot, which helps compliant applications, but flatten the folder structure as well - many older applications still cap at 260 regardless of the setting. Mapping a drive letter to a deep folder is a quick workaround.

feedback.note: enabled it and shortened two folder names

goal: Disk Management shows a healthy partition but Windows says the drive needs formatting
plan: Check what file system is actually reported
Confirm the partition table is intact
Decide whether formatting would lose data

steps.command: Get-Disk 2 | Select-Object Number, FriendlyName, PartitionStyle, OperationalStatus
steps.stdout:
Number FriendlyName    PartitionStyle OperationalStatus
------ ------------    -------------- -----------------
2      WD My Passport  GPT            Online

steps.command: Get-Volume | Where-Object DriveLetter -eq 'F' | Select-Object FileSystem, HealthStatus, Size

summary: The partition table is intact and the partition is the right size, but the volume reports no file system at all - the NTFS boot sector or MFT header is damaged. The data clusters are almost certainly still there; only the structure describing them is unreadable.
recommendation: Do not format. Image the drive first, then run read-only recovery tooling against the image - formatting writes a new file system over the structures a recovery tool would use to rebuild the old one. TestDisk can often repair the boot sector from its backup copy.

feedback.note: TestDisk rebuilt the boot sector, everything came back

goal: Wi-Fi works but only at a fraction of the speed the router should give
plan: Check the negotiated link rate against the standard
Look at the band and channel width
Identify the limiting factor

steps.stdout:
Radio type            : 802.11n
    Band                  : 2.4 GHz
    Channel               : 6
    Receive rate (Mbps)   : 72
    Signal                : 88%

steps.command: netsh wlan show drivers | Select-String 'Radio types supported'
netsh wlan show networks mode=bssid | Select-String 'SSID|Band|Channel' | Select-Object -First 6
steps.stdout:
SSID 1 : HomeNet
    Band : 2.4 GHz
    Channel : 6
SSID 2 : HomeNet-5G
    Band : 5 GHz
    Channel : 36

summary: The adapter supports Wi-Fi 6, but it has connected to the 2.4 GHz network at 802.11n, capping the link at 72 Mbps. Signal strength is fine at 88% - the limitation is the band, and a separate 5 GHz network is being broadcast that it has not joined.
recommendation: Connect to the 5 GHz SSID explicitly and set it to connect automatically. If the router presents both bands under one name, the adapter will often stick to 2.4 GHz because it has the stronger signal, even when 5 GHz would be far faster.

feedback.note: connected to the 5G network, went from 70 to 600 Mbps

goal: One background process writes to disk constantly even when the PC is idle
plan: Identify the process and its write volume
Determine what it is writing
Decide whether it is expected

steps.command: Get-Counter '\Process(*)\IO Write Bytes/sec' -MaxSamples 1 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty CounterSamples | Where-Object CookedValue -gt 100000 | Sort-Object CookedValue -Descending | Select-Object -First 3 InstanceName, CookedValue

summary: A vendor telemetry process is writing 4.8 MB per second continuously and has accumulated 8.4 GB of logs. This is not malware, but it is an unreasonable amount of background writing - on an SSD it also consumes write endurance for no user benefit.
recommendation: Check the vendor application's settings for a diagnostic or verbose logging option that has been left enabled, which is the usual cause. If there is no setting, the telemetry service can be disabled without affecting the application's main function.

feedback.note: debug logging had been left on since installation

goal: Windows Defender scans take hours and never seem to finish on this machine
plan: Check what the scan is covering
Look for paths that expand enormously
Identify the scope problem
summary: The full scan is covering 842 GB of virtual machine disks plus Docker data and backups, with no exclusions configured. Scanning inside a VHDX is largely pointless - the guest has its own protection - but it takes hours and rescans the whole file whenever the VM writes anything.
recommendation: Add the VM and Docker data folders to Defender's exclusion list, and consider excluding the backup destination too. Keep exclusions narrow and path-specific; excluding a whole drive would leave genuine user data unprotected.

feedback.note: scan went from 6 hours to 25 minutes

goal: Sound crackles only when I'm on battery, never when plugged in
plan: Check whether power management affects the audio path
Look at processor state on battery
Identify the mechanism

steps.stdout:
Current AC Power Setting Index: 0x00000064
Current DC Power Setting Index: 0x00000005

summary: On battery the minimum processor state is set to 5%, so the CPU drops to 800 MHz. Audio processing has hard real-time deadlines, and at that clock the driver cannot always fill its buffer in time - each missed buffer is an audible crackle. On AC the minimum is 100%, so it never happens.
recommendation: Raise the minimum processor state on battery to around 20-30% under the power plan's processor settings. That costs a little battery life but gives the audio path enough headroom; the audio hardware itself is fine.

feedback.note: 20% minimum on battery and the crackling stopped

goal: Text and windows are blurry after I undock the laptop
plan: Check the scaling on each display
Look at whether apps re-read DPI on change
Identify what needs to happen

steps.command: Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/wmi -ClassName WmiMonitorBasicDisplayParams | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count

summary: The external monitor ran at 100% scaling and the laptop panel needs 150%. Applications that are not per-monitor DPI aware keep rendering at the old scale and Windows stretches the result - so they look soft until they are restarted at the new scale.
recommendation: Close and reopen the affected applications after docking or undocking, or sign out and back in to reset everything at once. Applications that stay blurry even after restarting need the 'System (Enhanced)' high-DPI override in their compatibility settings.

feedback.note: restarting the apps fixes it, now I know why

goal: A service starts, stops immediately, and repeats forever
plan: Check the service state and its recovery configuration
Find why it exits
Break the loop before fixing the cause

steps.stdout:
Faulting application name: appmonitor.exe
Exception code: 0xc0000005 in config parser

summary: The service crashes in its configuration parser roughly every 30 seconds, and its recovery action restarts it each time - so the loop is the recovery policy working as configured on a service that cannot start. The crash is the cause; the loop is the symptom.
recommendation: Set the service to Disabled first to stop the churn, then fix or replace config.xml. Changing the recovery action to 'Take no action' after the first failure prevents this pattern from filling the event log while a real fault is present.

feedback.note: config file had been half-written during a crash

goal: Downloads start fast then slow to a crawl after a few seconds
plan: Check the TCP tuning settings
Look for a congestion or window scaling limit
Identify what throttles after the start

steps.stdout:
Receive Window Auto-Tuning Level : restricted
Add-On Congestion Control Provider : none
ECN Capability : disabled

summary: Receive window auto-tuning is set to Restricted, which caps how far the TCP window can grow. On a link with 84 ms latency the transfer starts at the initial window size then cannot scale up, so throughput collapses once the initial burst is done - exactly the pattern described.
recommendation: Set it back to normal with 'netsh int tcp set global autotuninglevel=normal'. Restricted is an old troubleshooting suggestion that actively harms high-latency connections, which is where window scaling matters most.

feedback.note: downloads went from 2 Mbps back to full speed

goal: Outlook keeps asking for my password over and over
plan: Check whether a stale credential is being replayed
Look at the authentication method in use
Identify what to clear

steps.stdout: The connection to Microsoft Exchange is unavailable. Outlook must be online...

summary: Two credentials exist for the same mailbox - an organisational one and a personal live.com one - and modern authentication is disabled by the EnableADAL=0 key. Outlook falls back to basic auth, the wrong cached credential is offered, the server rejects it, and the prompt reappears.
recommendation: Delete both Office credentials from Credential Manager and remove the EnableADAL value so modern authentication is used. Basic authentication is disabled on Exchange Online, so leaving ADAL off guarantees this loop rather than merely risking it.

feedback.note: cleared the credentials and it signed in once, properly

goal: Outlook is stuck on 'Trying to connect' but the internet works
plan: Check whether the mail endpoint specifically is reachable
Look at the autodiscover path
Distinguish general network from mail-service reachability
summary: The mail service is reachable on 443, so this is not connectivity. Outlook is configured to prefer a local Autodiscover XML file that does not exist, and the autodiscover DNS record is missing - so it never learns which server to talk to and sits at 'Trying to connect'.
recommendation: Remove the PreferLocalXML and ExcludeHttpsRootDomain values so Outlook uses the normal Autodiscover sequence, and have DNS publish the autodiscover CNAME. Rebuilding the profile would not help while these overrides point at a file that is not there.

feedback.note: leftover keys from an old migration script

goal: Sent emails sit in the Outbox and never leave
plan: Check whether the item is genuinely stuck or just large
Look at the send path
Identify the blocker

steps.command: Get-Process OUTLOOK -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Id, Responding, WorkingSet64

summary: Outlook is responsive and the server is reachable, but the OST has grown to 48 GB. Above roughly 50 GB the file becomes unstable and synchronisation stalls - the send queue is blocked behind a sync operation that cannot complete, not by a network fault.
recommendation: Reduce the mail-to-keep-offline window under Account Settings so the OST shrinks, then let it resync. Archive older mail to an online archive rather than a local PST; a PST on a network drive would create a different and worse set of problems.

feedback.note: cut offline mail to 12 months, OST dropped to 9 GB

goal: Search in Outlook returns nothing even for emails I can see
plan: Check whether Outlook is included in the index
Look at the index status
Identify what excludes it
summary: The search service is running and set up correctly, but a policy value explicitly prevents Outlook data from being indexed. Outlook then falls back to a client-side search that returns nothing for a cached mailbox of this size, which is why messages you can see are not found.
recommendation: Remove the PreventIndexingOutlook policy value and let the index rebuild - allow several hours for a large mailbox. Rebuilding the index first would have achieved nothing while the policy kept excluding the data.

feedback.note: a policy from an old GPO nobody remembered

goal: OneDrive says 'Processing changes' for hours and never finishes
plan: Check how many items are being tracked
Look for a file the sync engine cannot handle
Identify the stall point

steps.command: Get-Process OneDrive -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Id, CPU, WorkingSet64
Get-ChildItem "$env:USERPROFILE\OneDrive" -Recurse -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.FullName.Length -gt 240 } | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count

summary: OneDrive is tracking 412,000 files, well beyond the 300,000 it is designed for, and 18 folders have paths over 240 characters. It is not hung - it is churning through a set it cannot finish, and the over-length paths will fail even when it gets to them.
recommendation: Move the large archive folders out of OneDrive and keep them in a normal local folder or an offline archive. Shorten the deep paths as well. Resetting OneDrive is the usual first suggestion but it just restarts the same impossible scan.

feedback.note: moved a 200k-file photo archive out and it finished in 20 minutes

goal: Files show a cloud icon and won't open when I'm offline
plan: Check the Files On-Demand state
Look at whether the files are pinned
Explain the icon states
summary: Files On-Demand is enabled and this file carries the Offline reparse attribute - meaning it is a placeholder with no local content. That is the intended behaviour, not a fault: cloud-only files need a connection to download on first open.
recommendation: Right-click the folders you need on the road and choose 'Always keep on this device' before travelling. With 20 GB free there is room to pin a working set; pinning the entire OneDrive would fill the disk and cause a different problem.

feedback.note: pinned my current project folder, works offline now

goal: Two computers keep creating duplicate files with my PC name appended
plan: Confirm the pattern of the duplicates
Check what edits the file on each machine
Identify the conflict source

steps.command: Get-ChildItem "$env:USERPROFILE\OneDrive" -Recurse -Filter '*.xlsx' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object Name -match '-DESKTOP-' | Select-Object -First 2 Name, LastWriteTime
Get-Process EXCEL, OneDrive -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, Id

summary: The name-suffixed copies are OneDrive's conflict resolution: the same file was changed on two machines before either finished syncing, so rather than lose an edit it keeps both. It is data preservation working, not corruption - but 64 of them means the pattern is habitual.
recommendation: Close files fully on one machine and wait for the sync icon to show complete before opening them on the other. For files edited from both regularly, use the web or desktop app's co-authoring instead, which merges rather than forking.

feedback.note: was leaving Excel open on the laptop overnight

goal: My microphone works everywhere except in Teams
plan: Check the OS-level app permission
Confirm the device is not exclusively held
Identify the block

steps.command: Get-PnpDevice -Class AudioEndpoint | Where-Object FriendlyName -match 'Micro' | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
steps.stdout:
Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     Microphone (USB Audio Device)

summary: Microphone access is allowed globally, but there is a per-application Deny specifically for the Teams executable. Windows blocks the capture at the OS level, so Teams shows a device but receives silence - nothing inside Teams can override this.
recommendation: Set Teams to Allow under Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone, in the desktop-apps section at the bottom of that page. The global toggle being on is what makes this confusing; the per-app entry is separate and takes precedence.

feedback.note: the per-app list was below the fold, never saw it

goal: Teams screen sharing shows a black rectangle to everyone else
plan: Check which GPU renders the shared content
Look at hardware acceleration in the capture path
Identify the mismatch

steps.stdout:
Name                      Status
----                      ------
Intel(R) Iris Xe Graphics OK
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050   OK

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_PnPSignedDriver | Where-Object DeviceName -match 'NVIDIA' | Select-Object DriverVersion

summary: The shared application renders on the NVIDIA GPU while Teams is pinned to the integrated Intel GPU by an explicit preference. The capture path cannot read another adapter's framebuffer, so it sends black - which is why audio and everything else works.
recommendation: Set Teams and the application being shared to the same GPU in Graphics settings, or remove the override so Windows decides. This affects all hybrid-graphics laptops and is not a Teams bug; the same happens with other capture software.

feedback.note: set both to the same GPU and sharing works

goal: The scanner is detected but scanning fails with a communication error
plan: Check the imaging service state
Confirm the device driver stack
Identify the broken link

steps.stdout:
Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     Canon MF4700 Series

summary: The device is enumerated correctly, but the Windows Image Acquisition service is stopped and disabled. Every WIA scan request goes through that service, so scanning fails while printing on the same multifunction device keeps working - printing uses the spooler instead.
recommendation: Set stisvc to Automatic and start it. It is often disabled by 'services to disable' guides, which do not account for multifunction devices where the scan half depends on it and the print half does not.

feedback.note: a debloat script had disabled it

goal: Scanned PDFs come out enormous - 40 MB for a couple of pages
plan: Check the resolution the scan is being made at
Look at the colour mode
Identify what drives the size
summary: The scan profile is set to 1200 dpi in full colour, which is archival-photograph quality applied to text documents. Nothing is malfunctioning - each page is simply being captured at roughly sixteen times the data of a normal document scan.
recommendation: Set the profile to 300 dpi and greyscale for text, which is fully legible and produces files around 1 MB per page. Keep 600 dpi colour for photographs or anything that will be OCR'd from poor originals.

feedback.note: 300 dpi greyscale, files are 900 KB now

goal: Mobile hotspot turns on then switches itself off after a minute
plan: Check the hosted network capability
Look for a power-saving interaction
Identify what stops it

steps.command: Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object Name -match 'Local Area Connection\*' | Select-Object Name, Status, InterfaceDescription
steps.stdout:
Name                        Status InterfaceDescription
----                        ------ --------------------
Local Area Connection* 12      Up  Microsoft Wi-Fi Direct Virtual Adapter

summary: The hotspot shuts down because no client connects within the idle timeout, and the Wi-Fi adapter is additionally allowed to power down. Both push in the same direction: a hotspot with nothing attached is treated as idle and torn down.
recommendation: Set PeerlessTimeoutEnabled to 0 under the icssvc Settings key to stop the idle shutdown, and untick 'Allow the computer to turn off this device' on the Wi-Fi adapter. Connect a client promptly and neither would trigger.

feedback.note: needed the hotspot up before the other device booted

goal: Devices connect to my hotspot but get no internet
plan: Check whether sharing is bound to the right connection
Look at the shared adapter's addressing
Identify the break in the path

steps.stdout:
Name                       Status InterfaceDescription
----                       ------ --------------------
Ethernet                       Up  Realtek PCIe GbE
Local Area Connection* 12      Up  Wi-Fi Direct Virtual Adapter

steps.command: Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias 'Local Area Connection* 12' -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object IPAddress

summary: Clients receive the 192.168.137.x address so DHCP is working, and the sharing service is running - but no NAT translation exists, so traffic reaches the host and stops there. The connection is established but nothing is forwarded upstream.
recommendation: Turn the hotspot off and on to have Windows recreate the sharing configuration, which rebuilds the NAT rule. If it does not return, a third-party VPN or firewall that installs its own NAT is usually the reason it was removed.

feedback.note: the VPN client had taken over NAT, reconnecting fixed it

goal: The screen colours look wrong - everything is washed out or inverted
plan: Check whether a colour filter is active
Look at the night light setting
Identify which one is applied
summary: A colour filter is active with FilterType 1, which is the greyscale-family filter. Night light is not configured and the display adapter is healthy - the washed-out appearance is an accessibility filter applied system-wide, not a display or driver fault.
recommendation: Turn it off under Settings > Accessibility > Colour filters, or press Windows + Ctrl + C. That shortcut is easy to hit accidentally, which is the usual way this gets switched on without anyone realising.

feedback.note: the keyboard shortcut, hit it while copying something

goal: Windows reads everything out loud and I can't make it stop
plan: Identify which assistive feature is speaking
Check how it was started
Turn it off and prevent recurrence

steps.command: Get-Process Narrator -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Id, StartTime

summary: Narrator is running, launched by the Windows + Ctrl + Enter shortcut which is enabled. It is not set to start at logon, so it only appears when that key combination is pressed - which explains why it comes and goes rather than being constant.
recommendation: Press Windows + Ctrl + Enter to stop it now, and turn off the keyboard shortcut in Narrator settings if it keeps being triggered. Leave Narrator itself installed - disabling the shortcut is enough and keeps the feature available if it is ever needed.

feedback.note: turned off the shortcut, no more surprises

goal: Start menu search finds nothing, not even installed apps
plan: Check the search service and index size
Look for index corruption
Decide between repair and rebuild

steps.stdout: The search service has detected corrupted data files in the index. The service will attempt to automatically correct this problem.

summary: The service is running but the index database is only 12 MB and has not been written to since June - it is corrupt and the automatic repair is not succeeding. An index of this size holds nothing, which is why even application names are not found.
recommendation: Rebuild the index from Indexing Options > Advanced. It will take a few hours and search will be incomplete meanwhile. If it corrupts again within days, check disk health - repeat index corruption is often the first visible symptom of failing storage.

feedback.note: rebuilt overnight, search works again

goal: File search finds nothing in a specific folder but works elsewhere
plan: Check whether that location is in the indexed scope
Look for an exclusion
Explain the difference
summary: The folder carries the NotContentIndexed attribute, so the indexer skips it entirely. Search still walks the folder for file names in some views but never sees the contents - which is why searching for text inside those files returns nothing while other folders are fine.
recommendation: Clear 'Allow files in this folder to have contents indexed' in the folder's Advanced attributes, then add the location under Indexing Options. Expect it to take time to catch up on a large archive folder.

feedback.note: the attribute was set when the folder was copied from an old drive

goal: The clock keeps drifting even after I set it correctly
plan: Check the time service configuration
Look at what it is syncing against
Identify the failure

steps.stdout:
Leap Indicator: 3(not synchronized)
Stratum: 0 (unspecified)
Source: Local CMOS Clock

#Peers: 1
Peer: time.windows.com,0x9
State: Pending
Last Successful Sync Time: unspecified

summary: The service is running but has never successfully synced - it is falling back to the CMOS clock, which drifts by design. The peer is stuck in Pending, meaning NTP on UDP 123 is not getting through or the peer is unreachable.
recommendation: Confirm UDP 123 outbound is allowed, then re-register the service and force a resync. On a domain-joined machine also check it is syncing from the domain hierarchy rather than an external server - mixing the two causes drift of its own.

feedback.note: the firewall was blocking outbound NTP

goal: Websites give certificate errors and my clock is a day out
plan: Check the clock against the time zone and DST
Look at the CMOS battery evidence
Fix the cause not the symptom

steps.stdout:
Sunday, 16 August 2026 09:14:22

Id                       BaseUtcOffset
--                       -------------
GMT Standard Time             00:00:00
The system clock was set to an earlier time at boot.

summary: The clock resets to an earlier time at every boot and only corrects once NTP sync completes - which is after the browser has already made its first connections. Certificates appear not-yet-valid during that window. The pattern points at a dead CMOS battery.
recommendation: Replace the CMOS battery. Forcing a resync fixes it until the next shutdown, so it looks solved but recurs - which is why the boot log rather than the current time is what identifies this.

feedback.note: five-year-old desktop, new battery sorted it

goal: A saved password keeps being used even after I changed it
plan: List what is stored in the credential vault
Identify the stale entry
Remove rather than overwrite

steps.stdout:
Target: Domain:target=fileserver
    Type: Domain Password
    User: CORP\jdoe

Target: LegacyGeneric:target=fileserver
    Type: Generic
    User: jdoe
An account failed to log on. Status: 0xC000006A (bad password). Caller Process: explorer.exe

summary: Two credentials exist for the same target - a Domain Password entry and an older Generic one. Windows offers the generic one first, it carries the old password, and each attempt produces a bad-password failure. Changing the password in one place left the other behind.
recommendation: Delete both entries with cmdkey and let Windows prompt fresh. Do this promptly - repeated bad-password attempts from a stale credential are a common cause of accounts locking out for no obvious reason.

feedback.note: that explains the random lockouts too

goal: Face unlock falls back to PIN every time and re-enrolment won't stick
plan: Check the biometric device and service
Look at whether the enrolment survived
Identify what to re-establish

steps.stdout:
Status FriendlyName
------ ------------
OK     Windows Hello Face Software Device
The biometric template database could not be opened. Error: 0x80070002

summary: The camera and service are healthy, but the biometric template database cannot be opened - the enrolment data was invalidated by the update. Windows falls back to PIN because there is no usable template to match against, not because the hardware failed.
recommendation: Remove and re-enrol face sign-in under Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options. The old templates cannot be recovered and should not be - they are deliberately non-portable, which is part of why Hello data never leaves the device.

feedback.note: re-enrolled in a minute, working again

goal: A scheduled task shows 'Running' but never actually does anything
plan: Check the task's last run result and duration
Look at whether the instance is stuck
Identify what blocks completion

steps.command: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'NightlyReport' | Get-ScheduledTaskInfo | Select-Object LastRunTime, LastTaskResult, NumberOfMissedRuns
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'NightlyReport' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Settings | Select-Object ExecutionTimeLimit, MultipleInstances
Get-Process -Name report -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Id, StartTime, Responding

summary: Result 267009 means the task is still running - it started eight days ago and the process has been unresponsive since. The execution time limit is PT0S, meaning no limit, so nothing ever terminates it, and MultipleInstances=IgnoreNew means every subsequent run is silently skipped. That accounts for the 7 missed runs.
recommendation: End the hung process, then set a realistic ExecutionTimeLimit such as PT1H so a stuck run is killed rather than blocking every future one. A task with no time limit and IgnoreNew fails permanently after a single hang.

feedback.note: set a 1 hour limit, it self-recovers now

goal: A task works when I run it manually but fails on schedule with 0x1
plan: Compare the manual and scheduled execution contexts
Check the working directory and account
Identify the difference

steps.command: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'BackupScript' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Principal | Select-Object UserId, RunLevel, LogonType
steps.stdout:
UserId       RunLevel LogonType
------       -------- ---------
SYSTEM        Limited   Password

steps.command: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'BackupScript' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Actions | Select-Object Execute, Arguments, WorkingDirectory

summary: The action uses a relative script path with no working directory set. Run manually from the script folder it resolves; run by the scheduler it starts in C:\Windows\System32 where the file does not exist, and PowerShell exits with 1.
recommendation: Use the full path in the arguments, and set the working directory explicitly. Also note it runs as SYSTEM - if the script touches mapped drives or a user profile, those will not exist in that context even once the path is fixed.

feedback.note: full path sorted it, good catch on the SYSTEM context

goal: Right-clicking a file freezes Explorer for 30 seconds
plan: Enumerate the context menu handlers
Identify handlers pointing at unavailable resources
Confirm the delay source

steps.stderr: Cannot find drive. A drive with the name 'HKCR' does not exist.

steps.command: New-PSDrive -Name HKCR -PSProvider Registry -Root HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT | Out-Null; Get-ChildItem 'HKCR:\*\shellex\ContextMenuHandlers' | Select-Object PSChildName
steps.stdout:
PSChildName
-----------
EPP
OpenGLShExt
SharingPrivate
CloudSyncShell
ArchiverExt

steps.command: Get-Service | Where-Object DisplayName -match 'CloudSync' | Select-Object Name, Status

summary: Five third-party context menu handlers are registered, and one of them belongs to a cloud sync product whose service is stopped. The handler waits for a response from a service that will never answer, and Explorer blocks until that request times out.
recommendation: Either start the CloudSync service or unregister its shell extension. Uninstalling the product cleanly removes the handler; deleting the registry key by hand works too but leaves the product half-configured, so prefer the uninstaller.

feedback.note: uninstalled the old sync tool, right-click is instant

goal: Explorer opens a new window every time instead of using the current one
plan: Check the folder launch setting
Look at whether processes are separated
Identify the configuration
summary: 'Launch folder windows in a separate process' is enabled, which is why seven Explorer processes exist and each folder gets its own window. It is a stability setting, not a fault - one crashing window will not take the taskbar with it, at the cost of memory and this behaviour.
recommendation: Untick that option in Folder Options > View if you prefer single-window browsing. Keeping it on is reasonable if you work with unreliable shell extensions; it is a trade-off rather than something to fix outright.

feedback.note: turned it off, back to normal browsing

goal: Blue screen KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE happens randomly
plan: Check the bugcheck parameters
Look at what precedes each crash
Identify the faulting component

steps.stdout: The computer has rebooted from a bugcheck. The bugcheck was: 0x00000139 (0x0000000000000003, ...). A dump was saved in C:\Windows\MEMORY.DMP.

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_PnPSignedDriver | Where-Object { $_.DriverDate -lt '2019-01-01' -and $_.DeviceName } | Select-Object DeviceName, DriverVersion, DriverDate
steps.stdout:
DeviceName          DriverVersion DriverDate
----------          ------------- ----------
Virtual Audio Cable 4.15.0.0      2017-03-22

summary: Bugcheck 0x139 with parameter 3 is a list-entry corruption caught by kernel control flow guard - a driver damaged a kernel structure. There are no WHEA events, so this is not failing hardware, and one driver on the system dates from 2017.
recommendation: Uninstall the 2017 virtual audio driver and test. If the crashes continue, analyse MEMORY.DMP with WinDbg's !analyze -v to name the faulting module; 0x139 is almost always a driver, so replacing memory or reinstalling Windows would be premature.

feedback.note: virtual audio cable driver was the culprit

goal: Blue screen WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR at random with no pattern
plan: Check whether the hardware error logger recorded the source
Look at clock and voltage settings
Distinguish a component from a configuration

steps.stdout: A corrected hardware error has occurred. Component: Processor Core. Error Source: Machine Check Exception

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object CurrentClockSpeed, MaxClockSpeed, LoadPercentage

summary: WHEA is reporting machine check exceptions from the processor core, and the CPU is running at 5.3 GHz against a rated maximum of 4.7 - it is overclocked. Bugcheck 0x124 is the hardware telling Windows it produced an uncorrectable error, so this is not a software fault.
recommendation: Reset the BIOS to defaults, including any XMP or automatic overclocking profile, and test. If machine check exceptions persist at stock settings, the CPU or motherboard VRM needs investigating - continuing to run in this state risks silent data corruption in anything being written.

feedback.note: stock settings stopped the crashes, keeping it there

goal: Blue screen SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION only when I close a specific application
plan: Correlate the crash with the application
Check the named module
Identify the driver involved

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_SystemDriver | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'Running' -and $_.Name -match 'vpn|filter|capture' } | Select-Object Name, PathName

summary: Bugcheck 0x3B with an access violation means a kernel-mode routine faulted, and the crash reproduces on closing one specific application. A VPN filter driver is loaded, and filter drivers commonly fault when tearing down a connection at process exit.
recommendation: Update or remove the VPN client that owns vpnflt.sys and test the same close sequence. A reproducible bugcheck tied to one action is worth far more than a random one - it lets you confirm the fix rather than wait and hope.

feedback.note: old VPN client, updating it fixed the crash

goal: Store apps open then close instantly with no error
plan: Check whether the packages are registered correctly
Look at the app model events
Identify the failure point

steps.stdout:
Name                          Status InstallLocation
----                          ------ ---------------
Microsoft.WindowsCalculator       Ok C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\...
error 0x80073CF6: package could not be registered - access denied on package folder

summary: The package reports Ok but registration fails with access denied, and the WindowsApps folder is owned by Administrators rather than TrustedInstaller. Someone took ownership of that folder, which breaks the permissions the app model depends on.
recommendation: Restore ownership to NT SERVICE\TrustedInstaller and reset the inherited permissions on WindowsApps. Re-registering the packages will keep failing until the folder ACL is correct - taking ownership of WindowsApps is a common and damaging suggestion in older guides.

feedback.note: had taken ownership months ago to delete an app

goal: An application I uninstalled still shows in the Start menu and opens an error
plan: Check whether the product is genuinely gone
Look for a leftover shortcut
Clean up the remnant

steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Product -Filter "Name LIKE '%OldApp%'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name
Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs" -Recurse -Filter '*.lnk' | Where-Object Name -match 'OldApp' | Select-Object FullName

summary: The product is properly uninstalled and its executable is gone - only an orphaned shortcut in the user's Start menu folder remains, pointing at a path that no longer exists. That is why it appears in search and errors when clicked.
recommendation: Delete the shortcut folder from the user's Start Menu\Programs directory. Uninstallers that write shortcuts to the user profile after installing per-machine often miss them on removal, so this is common rather than a sign of a bad uninstall.

feedback.note: deleted the folder, gone from search too

goal: Two versions of the same program are installed and the wrong one opens
plan: List the installed versions
Check which one owns the file association
Correct the association

steps.command: Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' | Where-Object DisplayName -match 'PDF Editor' | Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion
steps.stdout:
DisplayName    DisplayVersion
-----------    --------------
PDF Editor      8.2.1
PDF Editor     11.0.4

summary: Both a 32-bit version 8 and a 64-bit version 11 are installed, and the .pdf association still points at version 8's ProgID. The newer installer did not take over the association, so double-clicking always opens the old build.
recommendation: Uninstall version 8 - keeping two versions of the same editor is the underlying problem - then set the default app for .pdf explicitly. If version 8 is needed for something specific, change the association through Settings rather than by editing the registry.

feedback.note: removed the old one, no reason to keep it

goal: The laptop shuts down at 30% battery without warning
plan: Check the reported versus actual capacity
Look at the wear level
Determine whether the gauge is wrong
summary: The battery holds 1,840 mWh of a designed 5,200 - about 35% of its original capacity. The percentage shown is a proportion of what it can currently hold, and the cells collapse under load well before that figure reaches zero, so the shutdown is abrupt.
recommendation: Replace the battery. Recalibrating the gauge would make the reported percentage more honest but cannot restore capacity - at 35% health the runtime you are seeing is what the cells can deliver.

feedback.note: four year old laptop, new battery ordered

goal: The PC wakes up seconds after I put it to sleep
plan: Find what last woke the machine
List devices permitted to wake it
Disable the specific one

steps.stdout:
Wake History Count - 1
Wake History [0]
  Wake Source Count - 1
  Wake Source [0]
    Type: Device
    Instance Path: PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_15F3...
    Friendly Name: Intel Ethernet Connection

HID Keyboard Device
Intel(R) Ethernet Connection I219-V
USB Input Device

summary: The Ethernet adapter is the wake source, and it is set to wake on any network pattern - not just a magic packet. Ordinary broadcast traffic on the LAN is enough to trigger it, which is why it happens within seconds every time.
recommendation: Turn off Wake on Pattern Match while leaving Wake on Magic Packet if you use Wake-on-LAN. Pattern matching is almost never what people want; magic packets are targeted and will not fire on background chatter.

feedback.note: disabled pattern match, sleeps properly now

goal: Internal sites resolve but only when I type the full name
plan: Check the DNS suffix search list
Compare short and full name resolution
Identify the missing suffix

steps.stderr: intranet : DNS name does not exist

summary: The suffix search list is empty and the connection has no connection-specific suffix, so short names are never expanded. The full name resolves correctly, confirming DNS itself is healthy - only the suffix appending is missing.
recommendation: Set the DNS suffix search list to corp.local, ideally through DHCP option 15 or Group Policy so every machine gets it. Setting it manually on one machine works but the next one to join will have the same problem.

feedback.note: DHCP wasn't handing out the domain suffix

goal: VPN connects but everything becomes slow, including local network
plan: Check the route table after connecting
Look at whether all traffic is being tunnelled
Identify the routing effect

steps.stdout:
InterfaceAlias NextHop     RouteMetric
-------------- -------     -----------
VPN Tunnel     0.0.0.0               1
Wi-Fi          192.168.1.1          25

summary: The VPN installs a default route with a lower metric than the physical adapter, so all traffic including local subnet access goes through the tunnel. That is full-tunnel mode working as configured - and the reduced MTU of 1300 adds fragmentation overhead on top.
recommendation: If the policy allows it, ask for a split-tunnel profile so only corporate ranges use the tunnel. Full tunnel is often a deliberate security decision, in which case the slowdown is the accepted cost and only the MTU is worth tuning.

feedback.note: security requires full tunnel, at least now I understand it

goal: Ethernet shows connected but with a 169.254 address
plan: Check the DHCP lease state
Test whether a DHCP server responds
Determine where the request fails

steps.command: Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias 'Ethernet' -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object IPAddress, PrefixOrigin, SuffixOrigin

steps.stdout: Your computer was not able to renew its address from the network (DHCP server). No response received.

summary: The link is up but negotiated at 100 Mbps on what should be a gigabit connection, and no DHCP server responds. That combination - degraded link speed plus no DHCP - points at the cable or port rather than at Windows: a damaged pair drops the link to 100 Mbps and can corrupt the DHCP exchange.
recommendation: Replace the cable and try a different switch port. If the address is obtained but the speed stays at 100 Mbps, the run itself is faulty; the APIPA address is a downstream symptom either way.

feedback.note: cable had been crushed under a desk leg

goal: Logging in takes five minutes but is instant for other users on the same PC
plan: Compare the profile sizes
Check for folder redirection or roaming
Identify what is loaded at logon
